news.Title: Tesla Isn’t a Hyperscaler. Why the AI Bears Are Misreading Its $5 Billion Capex Cut.
news.Content:
Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA) is spending less money than originally planned this year. And for investors who track how much money is being poured into artificial intelligence, that might sound like bad news.

But Tesla's decision to reduce its 2026 capital expenditure (capex) forecast by more than $5 billion isn't necessarily a warning about AI demand. In fact, it could be a smart move for the electric vehicle maker.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The reason is simple. Tesla doesn't need to build massive amounts of computing capacity to compete with Amazon , Alphabet , and Microsoft .

That's not its business.

Image source: Tesla.

Tesla is still all-in on AI

On Tesla's third-quarter earnings call , Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja announced the company reduced its 2026 capex forecast from more than $25 billion to approximately $20 billion.

The reduction doesn't mean Tesla is backing away from artificial intelligence. The company continues to develop its Full Self-Driving technology, expand its Cybercab robotaxi program , and work on its Optimus humanoid robots. All three projects require considerable investment. But they don't require Tesla to build the equivalent of Amazon Web Services or Microsoft's Azure.

Tesla needs computing power to train its AI models and improve its autonomous systems. It also needs manufacturing capacity to produce vehicles and robots, as well as the infrastructure to operate its planned robotaxi fleet.

Those investments serve a specific purpose: developing products and services Tesla can eventually sell to customers.

Tesla doesn't need to win the data center race

Cloud computing companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars building data centers to support AI workloads. Alphabet raised its 2026 capex forecast to $200 billion, while Amazon increased its spending plans to $220 billion.

The aggressive spending makes a lot of sense. Those companies are building computing infrastructure that supports their existing cloud businesses, serves external customers, and provides the capacity needed to meet growing demand for AI services. Tesla has a different business model.

That doesn't mean Elon Musk's company can stop investing in AI infrastructure. Training autonomous driving models requires enormous computing resources, and those requirements could increase as the company expands its ambitions.

Story Continues

But there's little reason for Tesla to match the spending of companies whose business is selling computing capacity. In fact, building more infrastructure than it needs would tie up capital that could be used to expand vehicle production, develop Optimus, or support its robotaxi business.

And with those businesses still developing, Tesla has good reasons to be selective about where its money goes.

Tesla's capex cut is good news for investors

Tesla posted $28.05 billion in revenue for the third quarter, essentially unchanged from a year earlier. Automotive revenue declined 3%, while operating margins narrowed from 5.8% to 2.6%. Those numbers demonstrate that Tesla can't rely on its automotive business to generate unlimited amounts of cash for new projects.

But even so, Tesla generated $1.53 billion in free cash flow during the quarter and ended September with more than $45 billion in cash and investments. Cutting back on unneeded spending will give Tesla more flexibility to work on its autonomous driving and robotics businesses.

And importantly, management hasn't suggested that its AI development plans are being scaled back. Taneja said capital spending is expected to increase in the coming years as Tesla expands robotaxi operations, Optimus manufacturing, and AI computing infrastructure.

So the reduction in this year's budget appears to be more about when Tesla spends money than whether it intends to make those investments.

For investors in Nvidia and other AI infrastructure suppliers, Tesla's decision also shouldn't be confused with a slowdown in hyperscaler spending. The companies building cloud computing infrastructure have different customers, different revenue opportunities, and much larger capital budgets.

Tesla's challenge isn't to build the world's biggest collection of data centers. It's to turn AI technology into profitable products. And if the company can accomplish that while spending $5 billion less than originally planned, shareholders have every reason to welcome the decision.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Title: Tesla stock leaves rest of the Magnificent 7 in the dust, surging to October's top spot
news.Content:
For most of 2026, Tesla has been the Magnificent Seven's minivan. In October, it's the only one leaving skid marks.

Tesla ( TSLA ) stock jumped about 5% Monday, its best day since early September and its highest close in about three months. The rest of Big Tech was a mixed bag, with Apple ( AAPL ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ), and Meta ( META ) all ending lower.

That leaves Tesla with two very different report cards. It's still down by double digits this year, the worst showing in the Magnificent Seven. But it's up by double digits in October, the best in the group, while Meta, Alphabet, and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are all lower for the month.

Tesla is breaking through a crowded spot on the chart

The stock opened above Friday's high — a gap — and pushed through the $386 area. That level is both Tesla's highest close of October and roughly its 200-day moving average , a long-term trend line many traders watch. Clearing both at once is what makes this a breakout.

Even so, Tesla remains about a fifth below its record close.

The SpaceX connection

The rally came alongside a Barclays upgrade betting that a Tesla merger with SpaceX ( SPCX ) would hand shareholders a takeout premium , as Pras Subramanian reported . Barclays raised its price target to $450 from $370. Musk confirmed last week that the two companies had formed independent committees to explore a combination, though no deal has been announced.

Tesla is already in on the joke. On Monday, its Robotaxi service switched on a bigger Houston service area shaped like a Starship rocket, announced with a "Houston, we have liftoff" post. "I swear it's just a coincidence 😂," Musk replied on X.

A combination wouldn't just bring rockets. On Sunday, Musk said SpaceX had closed $40 billion in debt financing to buy AI chips, and he also warned about neoclouds — rent-a-GPU cloud companies such as CoreWeave ( CRWV ) — as my colleague Ines Ferré reported . A merged company would share that chip bill.

Watch $386. Holding it keeps the liftoff on course, while a slide back below would turn Monday into a one-day pop. Above, the next stop is the low $450s, where Barclays' target and Tesla's 2026 closing high nearly overlap.

news.Title: Anthropic's IPO Keeps Founders in Control Through a "Founder LLC" Voting Structure
news.Content:
The initial public offering (IPO) queue just welcomed its most unconventional corporate creature yet. Artificial intelligence (AI) heavyweight Anthropic, the developer behind the Claude platform, officially filed its Form S-1 registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) today.

The filing sets the stage for a Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT. But beneath Anthropic's staggering compute numbers and explosive top-line growth lies a governance framework that should stop prospective shareholders in their tracks.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Silicon Valley has long treated public investors as passive passengers. Mega-cap innovators like Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), and Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) built modern market empires on dual- or triple-class equities. Their stock structures grant public buyers economic claims while effectively walling off boardroom power behind insider shares.

But Anthropic's proposed setup makes even those founder-friendly bastions look tame. Instead of merely weighting voting rights based on who owns the most stock, Anthropic is slicing ownership, shareholder voting, and board oversight into five distinct share classes.

Anthropic Share Class

Number of Shares

Economic Rights

Voting Power

Class A

Up to 300 billion shares

Standard

1 vote per share

Class E

Up to 30 billion shares

None

1 vote per share (special matters only)

Class F

50.1% of the total power in ordinary shareholder votes

Class N

Up to 100 billion shares

Class T

1 vote per share (Board elections only)

Data from Anthropic's S-1 filing.

The 4 Major Differences

1. A single "golden share" instead of billions of shares (Class F)

SpaceX and Meta are the same story. Musk and Zuckerberg both have total control over shareholder votes through their massive holdings of supervoting Class B shares. They have the option to convert these shares into common stock if they want to raise personal cash, but then they would gradually lose their voting power.

At Anthropic, the founders created Class F common stock consisting of a single share held by the founders' LLC. It has no economic rights (no claim to profits or dividends) but gives the co-founders 50.1% of the total vote on all general corporate matters. The vote counts of other classes don't even matter in most cases; Class F decides the outcome of simple-majority votes.

Story Continues

Class E is another voting-only stock, but holds no sway in ordinary shareholder votes. Instead, its holders control the structure of the Long Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), the Public Benefit Corporation (PBC) status, and changes to Anthropic's Charter. It's a safeguard against Class F holders restructuring the company at will.

2. The board has an outside "safety valve" (Class T & the trust)

Elon Musk is on the board of SpaceX. It's a controlled company, and the board reports directly to him on a supermajority basis.

At Anthropic, the LTBT is an independent body of AI safety, national security, and policy experts holding the Class T shares. Shares in this class have no financial claim but have the sole right to elect and remove a majority of the Board of Directors. The founders hold 50.1% of general shareholder voting power via Class F shares but cannot outvote or remove the board majority elected by the Trust.

3. Strategic cloud partners are boxed out of governance (Class N)

Big tech investors such as Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) and Alphabet invested billions in Anthropic over the years. To prevent major partners from gaining control of the board or triggering antitrust and regulatory issues, Anthropic created Class N common stock. Class N shares have full financial ownership but no voting rights.

4. Fiduciary duty: "Mission" over shareholder value (PBC status)

Meta and Alphabet are conventional corporations registered in Delaware, whose boards have a general fiduciary duty to create value for equity shareholders. SpaceX moved its registration to Texas in 2024.

Anthropic is registered in Delaware, but as a PBC. By charter, the board must balance financial return against the "responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity." If the Trust determines commercial profit conflicts with safe deployment, the Trust-controlled board can legally prioritize safety over stock returns.

Remember, the Trust holds Class T shares and can replace the Board of Directors if needed. That's real power.

The Bottom Line

Alphabet pioneered non-voting Class C stock to fund equity compensation without diluting its founders' majority control. Meta has adopted a similar blueprint, creating Class C shares to finance $140B in AI infrastructure and personal tax liabilities while permanently locking Mark Zuckerberg's 61% voting majority against outside dilution. And at SpaceX, Musk has total control as his high number of supervotes completely dominates the boardroom.

In Anthropic's proposed structure, the founders have 50.1% of operational votes via an empty economic shell (Class F) and have effectively handed ultimate board control to an independent safety trust (Class T). Public investors buying Class A get financial exposure to the business, but governance is forever in the hands of Class F and Class T holders.

At Anthropic, Wall Street gets to pick up the tab for the compute bills, but it will never get a seat at the table. Make sure you're OK with this structure before buying Anthropic shares.

news.Title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees as tech giant reshapes its workforce
news.Content:
Microsoft on Monday announced a new voluntary buyout program that will cover about 60,000 eligible employees who can choose to leave the company with financial support and other career planning resources.

The buyout program covers more than a quarter of Microsoft's global workforce, as the company said it had about 223,000 full-time employees around the world as of June 30, 2026, in its annual filing. The voluntary exit program was first reported by Business Insider and follows Microsoft's rollout of a voluntary retirement program earlier this year.

Amy Coleman, Microsoft EVP and chief people officer, said in a memo posted on the official Microsoft blog that the buyout program "reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter."

The company's voluntary exit program is time-limited and available to eligible employees at level 70 and below. Microsoft's announcement indicated that eligible employees would be notified via email about the details of their voluntary exit offer within a few hours of the announcement.

Microsoft President Says Ai Faces Fewer Safety Rules Than Milk In Call For Global Regulation

Some organizations within Microsoft are participating in the program, which covers eligible employees in the U.S., the United Kingdom, Canada and India.

Read On The Fox Business App

Microsoft indicated that the participation of different organizations within the company is based on each business unit's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.

Coleman added that the voluntary exit offer is new to Microsoft and that the company will learn from it and added, "At the same time, we'll keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft."

Microsoft Ceo Says Superintelligence Must Remain 'Under Human Control'

"There is no one-size-fits-all approach for every team or every employee," Coleman said. "These are a few of the ways we're trying to meet different business needs while continuing to create opportunities for our own people to grow and contribute."

"My promise is to continue to provide clarity, listen and learn and keep improving," she added.

Earlier this year, Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its U.S. workforce, or about 9,000 employees.

Microsoft Says Its Ai Tool Outperforms Generalist Doctors In Complex Diagnoses

It also announced cuts affecting about 4,800 jobs in July, or about 2.1% of the global workforce, as it overhauled its Xbox gaming business and divested up to five studios to boost returns in the division.

Microsoft and other tech giants are facing costly investments in the buildout of artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure like data centers and in the chips that are used to train models, which have prompted moves to cut costs in other areas of their operations.

news.Title: Should You Buy Amazon Stock Now or Wait for a Dip?
news.Content:
For not only years, but decades, Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) has been a top growth stock to buy and hold. It's generated massive returns for investors. But lately, that just hasn't been the case. In the past 12 months, it's up by just 11%. While that's a decent return, it trails the S&P 500 , which has risen by 13% during that time frame.

There's been a lack of excitement around the stock of late, and it's down 6% in the past six months. Should investors buy it right now, or hold off for an even greater dip in price before doing so?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Amazon.

This is not typical territory for Amazon stock to be in

In the past, it wasn't uncommon for Amazon's stock to trade at inflated multiples with respect to earnings. Paying more than 50 or 60 times earnings wasn't unheard of, given how much growth potential the company had. Today, however, it's trading at a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of just 20. And while it did get a boost from investment-related gains in its most recent results, even on a forward earnings basis, which factors in analyst expectations, its forward P/E multiple is still fairly low at 23.

Meanwhile, the company has continued to do well. When it released its second-quarter results in July, its sales were up a solid 20% and operating income was even more impressive, rising by 43% year over year. The growth hasn't dried up by any means. Meanwhile, the business still has plenty of opportunities for growth related to artificial intelligence (AI), which should lead to even better results in the future.

Investors may be less excited about the business due to the flurry of other AI stocks to choose from.

Has Amazon's stock become a bargain buy?

In five years, Amazon's stock has risen a relatively modest 47%. That includes, however, the crash that took place in 2022. With the company a leader in tech and AI innovation, it can make for a tremendous long-term buy, particularly given its reduced valuation .

While the stock may potentially go lower if there are concerns related to the tech sector as a whole and inflated levels of capital spending on AI, Amazon remains one of the best tech stocks to buy. Investors shouldn't assume a greater decline is coming for Amazon's stock, as it already looks like a great buy right now, and a rally may be overdue.

news.Title: Goldman Sachs Drops Stark Forecast for AI Stocks
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Goldman Sachs is warning that the artificial intelligence investment boom could reach a crucial turning point before 2026 ends, with the economic boost from hyperscaler spending expected to peak this quarter. The forecast raises an important question for investors in Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ), Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ), Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ), and other AI-linked stocks: Can earnings growth keep pace once the extraordinary acceleration in infrastructure spending begins to moderate?

According to Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius, the year-over-year change in hyperscaler investment as a share of U.S. GDP is expected to peak at approximately 1.5% in the fourth quarter.

That doesn't mean AI spending is about to decline.

Rather, it suggests that the incremental contribution of AI investment to economic growth could begin fading , even as technology companies continue pouring billions into data centers, chips, and computing infrastructure.

The scale of that spending remains extraordinary.

Major hyperscalers, including Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ), and Oracle ( NYSE:ORCL ), are projected to spend approximately $725 billion to $800 billion on capital expenditures this year, according to estimates cited in the report.

Goldman has also highlighted the stock market's importance to the broader AI investment cycle.

In an optimistic scenario, its analysis considers a 55% rise in AI-related stocks alongside 20% gains in other equities, potentially boosting consumer spending through increased household wealth.

However, those figures represent scenario assumptions, not the bank's baseline stock market forecasts.

What investors should watch next

The immediate test comes this week's Big Tech earnings.

Microsoft and Alphabet report October 28, followed by Amazon on October 29.

Investors should scrutinize capital expenditure guidance, cloud revenue growth, AI demand, and free cash flow to determine whether spending is producing adequate financial returns.

Goldman has separately estimated that hyperscalers may need approximately $300 billion in annual AI revenue to break even on their investments.

Ultimately, slower spending growth would not necessarily undermine AI's long-term potential. But it could challenge elevated valuations across the companies benefiting most from the infrastructure buildout.

news.Title: 1 Reason to Buy Meta Stock Now and Hold for the Long Term
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), the owner of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, makes nearly all of its money from ads. As of Oct. 22, the stock is down about 10% from its September high of $779.82. This is despite a strong third-quarter earnings report, with revenue growing 26% year over year.

One reason I see the dip as a buying opportunity is that Meta is building new revenue streams that could make it an even stronger business over time. Meta's non-ad revenue from its apps grew 59% to $1.1 billion. Management said this growth came mainly from WhatsApp paid messaging -- businesses paying to message their customers on the app -- and subscriptions.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Another non-advertising revenue stream is Meta One, a subscription service that unlocks extra features across the company's apps, which has passed 15 million subscriptions and trials. That's less than 2% of Meta's total revenue today, but it's growing more than twice as fast as the company overall.

The runway is long. Meta estimates at least 500 million small businesses use its apps to reach customers, a ready-made market for paid messaging and AI business tools. CFO Susan Li said the company is starting new AI businesses that could start contributing to revenue growth in 2027, with the potential to scale "meaningfully" over the long term.

The main near-term headwind for the stock is heavy spending: Meta plans to spend up to $145 billion on capital expenditures this year, but management expects strong revenue growth to continue in 2027.

Meta stock trades at about 19 times analysts' 2027 earnings estimate -- roughly in line with the S&P 500 's average forward multiple of 19.3. I believe that's a reasonable price for a business with a daily user base of over 3.6 billion and the ability to reach new users through AI services over time.

news.Title: AI Headlines Pile Up as Wall Street Navigates a Volatile Week
news.Content:
Things are happening, folks.

Anthropic officially filed for its IPO this morning, SpaceX secured $40 billion in debt financing for GPUs, Meta announced plans for a $95 billion equity offering, and concerns surrounding the neocloud industry continue to intensify.

And that's just the AI news.

We also have five major central banks meeting this week, including the Federal Reserve on Wednesday, followed by GDP and PCE inflation data on Thursday. Meanwhile, roughly 25% of the S&P 500 by market capitalization is set to report earnings, including three of the largest AI hyperscalers, the oil majors and several major pharmaceutical companies.

All of this comes as the major indexes are navigating elevated volatility, trading near the lower end of their recent ranges as the midterm elections approach and geopolitical tensions continue to rise.

There is a lot to cover, so let's get into it.

Image Source: TradingView

Anthropic Opens Its Books: The First Look at Frontier AI Economics

One of the biggest developments this morning was Anthropic's public S-1 filing, officially setting the stage for its initial public offering later this year. The company, best known for its Claude family of AI models, plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

The short version is that the numbers are quite good. Really, they're extraordinary.

Revenue increased from just $41 million in 2023 to $386 million in 2024, before surging to approximately $4.6 billion in 2025. In the first six months of 2026 alone, revenue reached $16.3 billion, roughly 14 times the level generated during the same period last year.

Of course, the company is spending enormous sums to support that growth, but the underlying business economics appear considerably more compelling than many had anticipated.

Anthropic reported a $693 million operating loss during the first half of 2026, narrowing sharply from $2.1 billion in the prior-year period. Gross margins are also reportedly approaching 85%, suggesting an increasingly attractive revenue model as the business scales.

There was also a staggering $80.7 billion net loss, but that figure is somewhat misleading. Roughly $72.4 billion came from a noncash accounting adjustment required to revalue outstanding convertible notes as Anthropic's valuation surged.

Meanwhile, the company reported an enormous $112.4 billion cash reserve as of June 30, alongside another $19.3 billion in short-term investments.

This was all better than I had expected.

For several years, one of the biggest uncertainties hanging over the AI trade has been the lack of visibility into the economics of the companies actually developing these frontier models.

Story Continues

We have been able to see the enormous revenues flowing to Nvidia, the semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure providers, but had very little insight into whether their customers were building sustainable businesses.

Now, for the first time, we have a detailed look at one of the leading AI developers, and the initial picture is encouraging.

There are still plenty of questions about future computing obligations, operating expenses and long-term profitability. But Anthropic's extraordinary revenue growth, improving operating results and substantial liquidity suggest the commercial opportunity is very real.

And as more of these businesses move toward public ownership, the additional transparency could remove a meaningful source of uncertainty surrounding the entire AI investment cycle.

SpaceX Raises $40 Billion While Neoclouds Struggle

SpaceX (SPCX) announced over the weekend that it had secured approximately $40 billion in debt financing to purchase AI chips, highlighting the extraordinary scale of investment still flowing into the industry.

The announcement follows SpaceX's third-quarter earnings report last week, which revealed an explosion in AI-related revenue that increasingly complements its established Starlink and rocket-launch businesses.

Of the approximately $14.6 billion in quarterly revenue, $7.56 billion came from its AI business, which expanded nearly tenfold year over year.

That diversification is becoming an increasingly important advantage.

Musk also had some interesting comments on X regarding AI infrastructure financing and the neocloud industry.

According to Musk, debt markets have become far less willing to lend to businesses without substantial revenue streams outside AI data centers. He argued that SpaceX was able to secure financing because of its investment-grade balance sheet and established Starlink and launch revenues.

He also predicted substantial failures and consolidation among the more than 200 neocloud operators, describing the coming shakeout as "guppy-level death and consolidation."

Those are pretty stark comments, but the market has already been signaling growing concerns about the industry's financial sustainability.

For those unfamiliar, neoclouds are specialized cloud computing businesses that build data centers and rent computing capacity to AI developers and enterprise customers.

Companies such as CoreWeave (CRWV), Nebius (NBIS) and IREN (IREN) have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom, but their expansion strategies require enormous amounts of capital, much of it financed through debt.

As interest rates have risen and lenders have become more concerned about the durability of these business models, the sustainability of that approach has come into question.

CoreWeave has been at the center of the turmoil.

Some of the company's unsecured bonds have fallen below 80 cents on the dollar, levels typically associated with distressed debt, while yields on certain issues have climbed above 15%.

That is a significant warning sign.

A company whose business model depends on continuously borrowing billions of dollars to expand computing capacity faces a much more difficult environment when lenders suddenly demand substantially higher returns.

CoreWeave and other neocloud operators have substantial contracted revenue backlogs, and demand for computing capacity remains extremely strong. That is the bullish side of the argument.

But strong demand does not necessarily guarantee a sustainable business model, particularly when financing costs, equipment depreciation and future capital requirements are all moving targets.

I continue to believe the AI infrastructure boom has considerable room to run, but the market is increasingly distinguishing between companies with strong balance sheets and established cash flows and those dependent on continued access to external capital.

That distinction could become one of the defining themes of the next phase of the AI investment cycle.

Meta Turns to Equity Markets to Finance Its AI Expansion

Also this morning, Meta Platforms (META) announced plans to raise as much as $95 billion through equity issuance to help finance its enormous AI expansion.

The announcement follows last week's earnings report, when Meta beat estimates on both the top and bottom lines and raised its expected 2026 capital expenditures to between $135 billion and $145 billion.

That is an extraordinary amount of money, even for a company of Meta's size.

The financing plan begins with approximately $35 billion in common and preferred stock offerings, followed by an additional $60 billion that could be raised through an at-the-market equity program next year.

What makes this development particularly interesting is the change in how Meta is financing its investments.

Until recently, the company had largely funded its capital expenditures through the enormous cash flows generated by its advertising business. Now, it is turning directly to shareholders for additional capital.

It is also a different approach from SpaceX, which has relied heavily on debt financing.

And Meta is not alone.

Alphabet (GOOGL) completed a similar $90 billion multi-tranche equity and equity-linked capital-raising program in June, including common equity, convertible preferred shares, a private placement and an at-the-market offering.

We are now seeing some of the largest and most profitable companies in the world turn to external financing to support their AI ambitions.

There is nothing inherently wrong with that. In fact, issuing equity can be a more conservative approach than taking on excessive debt, particularly when the returns on these investments remain uncertain.

But it does introduce dilution risk for existing shareholders, and it illustrates just how much capital the AI industry is consuming.

Another interesting detail is that Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom have reportedly expressed interest in purchasing up to $5 billion of Meta's offering collectively.

In other words, some of the companies supplying AI infrastructure are now potentially helping finance the customers buying their products.

Taken together, these announcements highlight an important evolution in the AI investment cycle.

For the last several years, the primary focus has been on how quickly companies can build out computing infrastructure. Increasingly, the questions are shifting toward how that expansion will be financed, what the capital will cost and whether the eventual returns will justify the investment.

The demand side of the equation still looks exceptionally strong. But financing is becoming an increasingly important consideration, and the market is beginning to take notice.

Five Central Banks, Three Days and Another Critical Fed Decision

Beyond the AI headlines, the macroeconomic calendar is exceptionally busy this week.

Five major central banks are scheduled to announce interest rate decisions over the next three days, including the Federal Reserve, Bank of Canada, Reserve Bank of New Zealand, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan.

The general expectation is for most policymakers to leave rates unchanged, although New Zealand and Canada could potentially deliver additional hikes.

In the United States, the Federal Reserve is widely expected to hold its benchmark policy rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, with fed funds futures pricing approximately an 89.5% probability of no change as of this writing.

That makes the decision itself somewhat less important than the accompanying commentary from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, although he has generally been reluctant to offer much in the way of explicit forward guidance.

The more important question is whether the Fed sees enough evidence of persistent inflation to justify another rate hike before year-end.

Recent economic resilience, rising energy prices and stubborn inflation pressures have complicated the outlook considerably.

And given the growing concerns surrounding debt-financed AI expansion, the direction of interest rates is becoming even more consequential for the technology sector.

We also have two important economic releases on Thursday morning, with the advance estimate for third-quarter GDP and the September Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation report.

The GDP report should offer another useful indication of the economy's underlying momentum, while PCE remains one of the Fed's preferred measures of inflation.

A hotter-than-expected inflation print immediately following Wednesday's Fed decision could quickly shift expectations for December and put additional pressure on the bond market.

With interest rates already elevated and financial conditions becoming more restrictive, these releases have the potential to generate meaningful volatility across asset classes.

Big Tech Earnings Take Center Stage

Finally, we have another exceptionally important week of corporate earnings.

The third-quarter reporting season is moving into full swing, with more than 130 S&P 500 companies expected to release results over the coming days.

Several of the world's largest technology companies will be reporting, including Alphabet, Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN).

Of course, investors will be watching the traditional metrics, including cloud revenue growth, operating margins, earnings guidance and the performance of each company's core businesses.

But I suspect the biggest questions will center around capital expenditures.

How much more are these companies planning to spend on AI infrastructure? Are they beginning to see meaningful returns from their investments? And perhaps most importantly, how much additional financing will they need to support their expansion plans?

After the developments at Meta, SpaceX and across the neocloud industry, those questions are likely to receive considerably more attention.

The hyperscalers have been the primary drivers of the enormous capital investment cycle supporting semiconductor manufacturers, data center operators, power infrastructure providers and countless other businesses.

As long as that spending continues to grow, it should remain a powerful tailwind for the broader AI ecosystem.

However, any suggestion that these companies are becoming more cautious could create another round of volatility, particularly among the more speculative infrastructure providers.

Outside technology, we also have major earnings reports from Eli Lilly (LLY), Mastercard (MA), Exxon Mobil (XOM) and Chevron (CVX), among many others.

Energy and technology have been major contributors to S&P 500 earnings growth, making these reports particularly important for assessing the strength of corporate profits.

I'll also be watching for continued signs of earnings growth broadening beyond the technology sector, which would be an encouraging development for the sustainability of the bull market.

What to Expect in the Stock Market This Week

There is a lot for investors to digest this week, and given the recent volatility, I wouldn't be surprised to see some sharp market reactions to the incoming headlines.

My broader outlook remains constructive. The AI infrastructure boom, substantial fiscal spending and relatively abundant liquidity continue to provide important support for economic activity and corporate earnings.

However, the latest financing developments are worth taking seriously.

The scale of capital investment is becoming extraordinary, borrowing costs are rising, and investors are beginning to distinguish more carefully between companies with sustainable cash flows and those heavily dependent on external financing.

I don't see these developments as evidence that the AI boom is ending. Rather, they suggest the investment cycle is entering a more mature and potentially more selective phase.

And despite the recent selling, there is still plenty of evidence that underlying demand remains exceptionally strong. Anthropic's financial disclosures were a particularly encouraging development on that front.

With central bank decisions, major economic reports and hyperscaler earnings all arriving over the next few days, we should have a much clearer picture of where the market stands by the end of the week.

For now, I think patience and selectivity remain important. We could certainly see additional volatility as the midterm elections approach, but I continue to believe the underlying bull-market drivers are intact.

And if those fundamentals continue to hold up, the recent selling could ultimately create some very attractive opportunities.

news.Title: Nvidia Just Gave a Huge Catalyst to This AI Stock. How to Play AMBA Stock Here.
news.Content:
An American fabless semiconductor company, Ambarella (AMBA), suddenly becomes the most interesting stock in edge AI. On Oct. 21, a post from Betaville suggested Nvidia (NVDA) could be the third party to buy the edge-AI chipmaker, after NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) and Qualcomm (QCOM).

The company was said to be getting the same advice from Goldman Sachs, which was also reportedly looking at a potential sale, but there has been no official bid, price, or deal announced.

More News from Barchart

How to Play RKLB Stock as Rocket Lab Pushes Its Neutron Launch to Next Year

Morgan Stanley Sees Amazon Stock Surging 100% with AWS Hitting $1 Trillion in Revenue Sooner Than People Think

Dell, Lenovo, Cisco, HPE, Supermicro: Why AMD's New AI Blueprint Has Everyone Signing On

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

The impression of strategic logic appears to be correct: Ambarella offers low-power processors that, for example, analyze video and operate AI in cars, cameras, or robotics applications, while Nvidia would appear to be the leader in AI computing in data centers.

The acquisition of Ambarella could expand Nvidia's reach in physical AI and edge computing. Now unless a serious offer materializes, or if the talks go stale, those rumored gains could disappear just as fast as they came.

While investors might be tempted to be drawn into a possible bid, a more important question is whether Ambarella can generate yet more revenue and cash flow to support this valuation without being simply taken over.

A Rough Year for AMBA Stock

AMBA stock is down 6% year-to-date (YTD) in 2026, and it is down roughly 31% from its 2026 high. The stock rallied about 8% in late October on the Nvidia rumor, but that pop did not erase the earlier losses.

The negative catalysts were slow X7 adoption and margin pressure from rising memory costs. The positive catalyst is the buyout interest from three credible suitors. Without the M&A bid, the stock would likely be much lower.

Turning to valuation, Ambarella trades at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 6x. That is below its own historical median of 8x and below the semiconductor industry median. The forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 81.97. That looks expensive. But it reflects a depressed earnings base. On sales, the stock looks fairly valued on the slightly cheap side. On earnings, it is expensive. The market is pricing in a lot of future growth.

Story Continues

Why Nvidia Makes Sense as a Suitor

So the chip giant Nvidia is reportedly interested in the acquisition of Ambarella, with Goldman Sachs on board for the deal. Ambarella is the tech company that specializes in low-power AI chips for cameras, cars, and robots. That's the tangible aspect of AI. Currently, AI training in the data center is dominated by Nvidia. By acquiring Ambarella, Nvidia will gain a better position in the field of AI inference in actual devices.

Being the third bidder in the process, and the one with the largest purse, also increases the chances of getting a better deal. Theoretically, it is a good strategy. However, it is all still just a rumor. Traders are betting on a maybe and not something even remotely set in stone. This is why AMBA stock is still trading well below its YTD level despite the rally.

After that is the newest big move: the launch of the X7 AI accelerator. Ambarella announced the X7 on Sept. 15, 2026. It is designed for edge infrastructure and is extremely power-efficient and memory-consuming. It's also entered into seven-year distribution deals with Macnica and Capgemini (CGEMY). The opportunity from those deals would drive up to $500 million in incremental revenue over seven years. The moves illustrate that Ambarella has a larger enterprise going on the buyout side. The distribution deals expand the moat.

Q2 Was a Record Quarter

Ambarella's fiscal second quarter of 2027 reported solid growth due to higher demand for its edge AI chips in the automotive and Internet of Things (IoT) segment.

Revenue increased by 13% over the prior-year figure to $108.1 million and above management's guidance as well. Solid sales of commercial vehicles and edge artificial intelligence revenue helped handily. The enterprise IoT segment also performed better than the consumer-focused segments.

Profitability went up as well. Ambarella registered a net loss of $6.7 million, compared to a $20 million loss a year ago. Adjusted net income was $8.2 million, or $0.18 per share, in the current quarter compared to $8,200,000, or $0.15 per share, for the same quarter last year.

But the free cash flow was negative at $7.1 million. At the end of the quarter, the company had $272.3 million in cash and marketable securities for financial flexibility as the company started to invest in new products.

CEO Fermi Wang was upbeat. "Our edge AI revenue reached record levels in Q2, with balanced sequential growth in Auto and IoT markets," he said. He also highlighted the X7 launch and the new distribution deals.

For the coming fiscal 3Q results, Ambarella is forecasting $115 million to $124 million in revenue and gross margins from 59% to 60%. Analysts are estimating fiscal 2027 revenue at about $440.6 million and adjusted earnings per share at a loss of $1.12, so higher revenue can be expected if sales demand continues.

Wall Street Is Split on AMBA Stock

Wall Street opinion towards AMBA stock is generally mixed but leaning positive. Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore has a "Buy" rating and a $96 price target. Roth Capital cut its target to $65 with a "Neutral" rating. Bank of America lowered its target to $70 with a "Neutral" rating.

The consensus rating among 13 analysts is "Moderate Buy." The mean price target is nearly $90, implying about 35% upside from the current price.

Summing it all up. I think the stock is considered binary risk. A buyout may result in a premium. In the absence of an agreement, the stock may revert to a loss-making estimate. As one analyst said, "…there is a two-way risk for investors here, either a premium on the deal, or the valuation hitting loss warrant levels." This is the debate in a nutshell.

Currently, the only thing that's seriously driving AMBA stock is the buyout chatter. However, the core business is improving. The investors who purchase AMBA are now hoping there will be a deal. They are also taking a keen bet on the edge AI story continuing to go up. Either wager is a winner. Neither is guaranteed.

news.Title: News Failure: Neocloud Stocks Defy Musk's Warning
news.Content:
Understanding the Neocloud Debt Concerns

Until recently, Neoclouds, specialized cloud computing providers built specifically for artificial intelligence, have been among the best-performing stocks on Wall Street. However, over the past few weeks, investors in Neocloud stocks such as Nebius Group ( NBIS ), IREN ( IREN ), and CoreWeave ( CRWV ) have endured immense selling pressure and volatility amid rising debt concerns.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Caused Neocloud Stocks to Plunge?

On October 14th, CoreWeave shares fell more than 15% as bond yields jumped to distressed levels and Gartner warned of potential for slowdowns in AI infrastructure spending. After the initial pressure, a second wave hit after Meta Platforms ( META ) reported its first negative free cash flow quarter as a public company, sparking Wall Street concerns about the growing mismatch between massive Capex spending and cash flow.

Musk Sounds the Alarm on Neocloud Stocks

Over the weekend, Elon Musk sounded the alarm on pure-play Neocloud companies, saying:

"As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers. SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we're investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue. That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through but not many."

News Failure: Neoclouds Rally Despite Musk Warning

Seasoned investors know that monitoring price action relative to the news is more valuable than monitoring the news alone. Historically, stocks bottom on bad news. For example, on March 18th, 2020, billionaire investor Bill Ackman appeared on financial news TV and warned that "Hell is coming!" due to COVID-19 lockdowns. Three days later, the stock market bottomed and never looked back.

Image Source: TradingView

Monday's action in Neocloud stocks eerily mirrors Bill Ackman's warning during COVID. Most investors would assume Neoclouds would plunge further after Elon Musk's dire warning. However, on Monday, Neocloud stocks delivered a classic expectation breaker, ripping from red to green, and setting the stage for a potential bottom.

Bottom Line

While tighter debt markets and heavy capital expenditures pose a real hurdle for pure-play Neoclouds, market history suggests the worst fears may already be priced in. The surprising resilience of Neocloud shares after high-profile warnings mirrors past market bottoms, when asset prices reversed course just as headlines seemed most dire.

news.Title: Meta Stock Alert: Meta: The $25 Billion Legal Blow Investors Cannot Ignore
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (META) just got handed a massive $25 billion legal bill. A New Mexico judge recently ordered the tech and e-commerce giant to pay up after a jury found the company violated state consumer protection laws related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

That blow hit when shares are already under extreme pressure, down 22% over the past year and roughly 6% in 2026. Shares dropped more than 5% despite a Q3 earnings beat, which brought the one-month drop to near 15%. But here is the thing.

More News from Barchart

How to Play RKLB Stock as Rocket Lab Pushes Its Neutron Launch to Next Year

Morgan Stanley Sees Amazon Stock Surging 100% with AWS Hitting $1 Trillion in Revenue Sooner Than People Think

Dell, Lenovo, Cisco, HPE, Supermicro: Why AMD's New AI Blueprint Has Everyone Signing On

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

However, the positive thing is that the company's core business is still growing fast. So is this little selloff a buying opportunity? Let's try to find out.

The Legal Hit and What It Means

The New Mexico judge ordered a fine of $25 billion from Meta after a jury ruled the company broke the state Consumer Protection Act in the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Meta is appealing the penalty, saying it's unconstitutional and that it'll likely be thrown out in appeals court.

It's quite a judgment, though it could be more or less impactful based on the appeals path taken. Investors' sentiment has been dampened by broader privacy and child-safety legal liability on top of the settlement previously agreed by Meta to settle a lawsuit filed by a multistate coalition against Cambridge Analytica.

The big question now is how many other states will follow suit and add to Meta's legal expenses? The company had ample liquidity, with $44.5 billion in cash and cash equivalents, to buffer it against a financial storm.

And the ruling on its own does not destroy the foundational ads business for Meta. So despite the high cost, this isn't a serious threat to its ads business. However, the key thing investors need to watch out for is if these growing legal fees become a priority over business performance.

Meta's Latest Earnings Show a Business Is Booming

Meta delivered a strong third quarter, with revenue and adjusted earnings beating Wall Street expectations.

Revenue climbed 26% year-over-year (YoY) to $64.6 billion, topping analysts' consensus estimate of $63.37 billion. Advertising remained the company's biggest growth engine, with sales rising 26% to $63.1 billion.

Story Continues

However, profit was hit due to some ongoing legal issues. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $7.40, well above the $5.75 analysts had expected. However, Meta reported net income of $9.9 billion after recording a $9.9 billion legal settlement charge.

The bigger concern was cash flow. Free cash flow turned negative at $2.1 billion, marking Meta's first negative quarterly reading since its 2012 IPO. Capital expenditures jumped 80% to nearly $35 billion, and management raised the lower end of its full-year spending outlook, now expecting capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion.

Meta is pouring billions into AI infrastructure, betting that the investment will fuel future growth. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, pointing to annual growth of 22% to 27%.

For investors, it's not clear. While the advertising business is still robust, the costs of artificial intelligence and the business's faltering cash flow pose the question of how much the company will need to spend before those investments start paying off.

The Muse AI Story Is Real

Meta introduced its AI agents under the name of "Muse" in September. Muse has already been used by more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada. Approximately 25% of users interact with it every day. If that's the case, then Zuckerberg claims Muse will be able to earn more money per user than the entire Family of Apps.

The firm also said it'll carry out a two-for-one split of its stock using a new class of non-voting shares. The stock is to be distributed in the first of 2027. This doesn't alter the stock's true value but will result in a more attractive stock price and provide discounted liquidity for acquisitions and payroll to META stock.

Analysts See Major Upside for META Stock

Despite all of these worrying signs, Wall Street is not blinking. The consensus rating is still a solid "Strong Buy." The 12-month average price target sits at $855.67, implying 34% upside from here.

Separately, Goldman Sachs has a "Buy" rating and raises its price target to $885. Analyst Eric Sheridan says the risk-reward skew remains positive. "We still see a positive risk/reward skew on current shares when measured against the core business operating momentum," he wrote.

JPMorgan is even more bullish. Doug Anmuth raised his target to $940. He calls this the first quarter where Meta's "superintelligence" vision met "early product momentum."

Morgan Stanley keeps an "Overweight" rating and an $820 target. The firm calls Meta the "cleanest consumer GenAI winner." Barclays raised its target to $880. Analyst Ross Sandler says, "Muse is off to a great start and represents a game changer for the META narrative."

Meta trades at a forward P/E of 19 based on 2027 estimates. The sector median is closer to 28. That looks cheap for a company growing revenue north of 20%. The legal bill is huge. The AI spending is huge. But the core ad machine is still humming.

From my perspective, Investors with a long horizon should see this dip as an opportunity, not a trap.

news.Title: How to Play Amazon Stock Before Q3 Earnings as the AI Trade Flounders
news.Content:
The Q3 2026 earnings season for "Magnificent 7" stocks is looking a lot like the previous quarter. In a reminiscence of the Q2 earnings season, both Tesla (TSLA) and Meta Platforms (META) plunged following their respective Q3 earnings last week, taking down the entire artificial intelligence (AI) universe with them. The earnings season gains pace this week, with Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) releasing their September quarter reports.

Tech Stocks Have Weakened as AI Trade Flounders

In the last earnings season, Microsoft gained the most among its Mag 7 peers following its confessional. The stock continued to build on the gains and rose an impressive 38% in Q3, clocking its best quarter since 1998. It went on to hit its record closing high last Tuesday and reclaimed its $4 trillion market cap before earnings from fellow Mag 7 companies dampened sentiment.

More News from Barchart

How to Play RKLB Stock as Rocket Lab Pushes Its Neutron Launch to Next Year

Morgan Stanley Sees Amazon Stock Surging 100% with AWS Hitting $1 Trillion in Revenue Sooner Than People Think

Dell, Lenovo, Cisco, HPE, Supermicro: Why AMD's New AI Blueprint Has Everyone Signing On

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

Amazon's story has been a bit different from Microsoft's, and it failed to hold onto its post-Q2 earnings gains. In a previous article, I noted that investors shouldn't expect a big rally in MSFT stock following its fiscal Q1 2027 earnings. Let's dive into how to play Amazon stock as the AI trade flounders.

What to Expect From Q3 Earnings

Amazon guided for Q3 revenues to rise between 9% and 12% year-over-year (YoY). Analysts are modelling the company's Q3 earnings per share (EPS) to rise 30.8%. During the Q3 earnings call, enterprise-focused Amazon Web Services (AWS) and the AI business, including the chip segment, would garner most attention. However, I would also watch the commentary on consumer health, given the deteriorating macro environment. Consumers globally have been hurting from higher inflation, particularly elevated energy prices, which is taking a toll on discretionary spending. To make things worse, interest rates are on an upward trajectory, hurting the monthly budgets of many middle-and-lower income families.

How Do Analysts Rate AMZN Stock Before Q3 Earnings?

Sell-side analysts have mostly made cursory adjustments to Amazon's target price—both on the upside and downside—ahead of its Q3 earnings. There have been some notable changes, though. For instance, famed tech analyst Dan Ives initiated coverage on Amazon at his recently formed Yorkville Ives with an "Outperform" rating and a $300 target price, while Tigress Financial analyst Ivan Feinseth raised the stock's target price from $315 to $385.

Story Continues

Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak named Amazon as a Top Pick and believes AI could drive AWS revenues to over $1 trillion. As a note of caution, Amazon has been a "top pick" for analysts for the last few years, but the stock hasn't been able to live up to expectations. AMZN stock is up around 47% over the last five years, which trails not only the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) but also the more diversified S&P 500 Index ($SPX). In fact, among its Mag 7 peers, AMZN is the second-worst performer and has fared better than only Tesla, whose shares are almost flat over the period.

How to Play Amazon Stock?

I have been bullish on Amazon stock this year and maintain my stance as the Andy Jassy-led company heads into its Q3 confessional. There are legit concerns about agentic AI negatively impacting Amazon's lucrative digital advertising business, and the company's once-enviable free cash flows are falling prey to burgeoning AI capex. Furthermore, the growth in the company's e-commerce operations in developed markets has slowed.

I, however, believe the risks are overblown and markets are overlooking the AI opportunity, including from third-party chip sales. In the e-commerce business, competition from the likes of Walmart (WMT) is rising, but Amazon has built an enviable ecosystem that is challenging to emulate.

Amazon's business has several moving parts, like Prime and digital advertising, that complement each other. Despite concerns about some aspects of its business, Amazon has a reasonably strong outlook, with AI being an enabler of both topline and bottomline growth.

In terms of valuation, AMZN stock trades at 23.2x its expected 2027 EPS, which is quite attractive. I remain invested in Amazon and believe the recent weakness in the stock, coupled with tepid valuations, raises the possibility of a post-earnings rally unless the company comes up with dud numbers.

news.Title: Anthropic is leasing data centers to reduce reliance on Amazon, Google, others
news.Content: Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) says it is increasingly leaning into leasing AI data centers to power its vast computing needs. The company calls the initiative Anthropic Direct and says that it helps address its compute requirements beyond simply leasing capacity from cloud service providers such as Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), according to Anthropic's S-1 investor prospectus, which it made public Monday . "As our compute requirements have scaled, we have transitioned to a hybrid model in which, in addition to purchasing compute as a cloud service, we also procure specialized AI accelerators directly and operate this hardware in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification," the company says. The move could also provide long-term economic advantages, according to Anthropic. In November 2025, the company announced a $50 billion investment that will see Fluidstack build data centers in Texas and New York through which Anthropic will lease computing capacity. The company says it is also directly leasing data center capacity and plans to sign additional agreements going forward. The moves make Anthropic a major player in the data center space, but also come at a time when the facilities continue to draw backlash from communities across the country over concerns about air and noise pollution and water usage. Towns and counties throughout the US have issued moratoriums or outright bans on developing data centers in their regions. New York has issued a one-year, statewide moratorium, while Texas has halted data center permitting until it can determine the impact the power-hungry sites will have on its grid. Key risk factor Anthropic lists the threat of further moratoriums on data centers as a key risk factor for the company in its prospectus. "Opposition to data center development has also become more organized and coordinated across jurisdictions, and our public profile may draw particular attention to projects associated with us," the company wrote in its S-1. "The loss of, or a significant disruption at, any major facility may not be readily absorbed by our remaining or future infrastructure. We are expanding our data center capacity internationally as part of our efforts to diversify our infrastructure footprint and reduce concentration risks associated with operating a significant portion of our compute infrastructure in the United States and to support our international growth strategy," Anthropic added. Data centers have also become a key topic in the 2027 midterms, with voters on both sides of the aisle expressing disapproval. news.Title: RDDT Rides on Strong Demand in Ad Business: Can It Beat META and SNAP?
news.Content:
Reddit RDDT is benefiting from a unique position in the digital advertising landscape, especially as it strengthens its ad game against major competitors like Meta Platforms META (Facebook/Instagram) and Snap SNAP.

A major driver of Reddit's advertising success is its robust financial and user growth. In the second quarter of 2026, Reddit posted its eighth consecutive quarter of more than 60% revenue growth, with advertising revenue up 64% year over year to $762 million. The platform now reaches more than 0.5 billion people weekly, including more than 130 million daily users. Notably, new app user retention improved 50% year over year, suggesting product enhancements are driving deeper engagement and higher-quality user growth.

The company's ad-stack innovation has been a major growth driver. The launch and rapid adoption of Reddit Max, an AI-driven suite for ad automation and optimization, has delivered significant results. Advertiser usage of Max grew by more than 60% from the first quarter, and revenues from Max campaigns increased by more than 150%. Features like tailored creatives and dynamic product ads are helping brands achieve better outcomes, such as Lenovo's 40% higher purchase value with Max campaigns compared to standard campaigns.

RDDT's expanding portfolio has been a major growth driver. Reddit recently introduced enhanced lead-generation capabilities to help advertisers convert high-intent engagement into qualified business opportunities. The enhancements include Max campaigns for automated optimization, in-market audiences targeting potential buyers and expanded audience and measurement integrations with Bombora, Demandbase, Clay, G2, Octane11 and Dreamdata. Reddit is also testing HubSpot integration to improve CRM workflows, attribution and reporting. These enhancements are expected to strengthen Reddit's advertising platform, improve campaign performance and drive advertiser engagement.

With ongoing investments in product innovation, user experience and ad technology, Reddit is poised to capture more advertising dollars and further strengthen its position against Meta Platforms and Snap in the digital ad market. For the third quarter of 2026, management expects revenues between $860 million and $870 million, representing 47% to 49% year-over-year growth. The midpoint implies about 48% year-over-year growth.

How Competitors Fare Against RDDT

Despite Reddit's expanding portfolio, the company faces stiff competition from Meta Platforms and Snap. Both Meta Platforms and Snap are also expanding their footprint in the rapidly growing digital ad market.

Meta Platforms is benefiting from strong advertising demand and improving monetization. In the third quarter of 2026, Meta Platforms reported advertising revenues of $63.1 billion, up 26% year over year. Total ad impressions increased 10%, while the average price per ad rose 14%, reflecting improving advertising performance and engagement. Meta Platforms' Family of Apps reached 3.64 billion daily active people, highlighting its extensive advertising reach.

Snap's strong advertising revenue has been a major growth driver for the company. In the second quarter of 2026, Snap's advertising revenues rose 9% year over year to $1.28 billion, reflecting improved momentum with large advertisers in North America, broader adoption of the company's AI-powered Smart Campaign Solutions and continued strength among small and medium-sized businesses.

news.Title: DoorDash Eyes Instacart Deal With Amazon in Crosshairs
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Instacart (CART) could be headed toward a multibillion-dollar takeover , with Wall Street analysts increasingly viewing DoorDash ( NASDAQ:DASH ) as a natural buyer in a potential deal that could create a stronger competitor to Walmart (WMT) and Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) in grocery delivery. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with DASH. Is DASH fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Instacart operates an online grocery marketplace connecting shoppers with retailers, earning revenue from delivery transactions, advertising, and technology services. Its extensive retailer partnerships make it an attractive acquisition target as competition in online grocery shopping intensifies. According to reports, Instacart has explored a potential sale and held preliminary discussions with both DoorDash and Uber (UBER), although Uber has reportedly walked away from negotiations. No agreement has been announced. Wells Fargo analyst Ken Gawrelski sees considerable strategic appeal, describing Instacart as an attractive asset supported by strong growth, healthy margins, and a valuation of roughly nine times projected 2027 EBITDA. Citi analyst Ronald Josey, meanwhile, expects Instacart's gross transaction value to reach $42.3 billion in 2026 , representing 13.6% annual growth, supported by approximately 370 million orders. Those figures help explain why DoorDash might be interested. Combining its delivery network and customer base with Instacart's grocery relationships could improve scale and strengthen its competitive position against Amazon and Walmart. A potential transaction could value Instacart at $16 billion to $17 billion , or approximately $65 per share, according to takeover estimates. However, those figures are speculative rather than a formal acquisition offer. What investors should watch next For Instacart shareholders, the obvious catalyst is whether DoorDash advances beyond preliminary discussions and submits a formal bid. Regulatory scrutiny remains a major risk, particularly given the overlap between the companies' grocery delivery operations. Meanwhile, Instacart's November 5 earnings report offers an important fundamental checkpoint. Management previously guided to third-quarter gross transaction value of $10.3 billion to $10.55 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $320 million to $340 million . Investors should watch order growth, advertising performance, and profitability to judge whether Instacart can sustain its momentum independently of a takeover. DoorDash reports earnings November 4, potentially offering additional clues about its acquisition priorities. news.Title: Anthropic makes more per employee than every Magnificent Seven company but Nvidia
news.Content:
Anthropic's headcount nearly tripled in a year. Its revenue grew 13x.

That pushed the AI lab's revenue per employee over the past year to more than $6.6 million, up from $1.4 million a year earlier, according to the IPO prospectus it filed Monday . Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) had about 5,300 employees as of Sept. 30.

Only Nvidia does better

Nvidia ( NVDA ) brings in about $7.2 million per employee, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Meta ( META ) is at $3.6 million. Apple ( AAPL ), at $3.1 million, brings in less than half as much per worker as Anthropic. Amazon ( AMZN ), with more than 1.5 million workers, is at $0.5 million.

This measures sales, not profit. Warehouses and retail stores swell Amazon's and Apple's payrolls. And Anthropic rents most of its computing, so many of the people running its data centers work for Google and Amazon .

The prospectus credits Claude, its AI model, for some of the leanness. More than 90% of the code added to Anthropic's codebase in September was written by Claude, the company said. That helped revenue climb from $41 million in all of 2023 to $16.3 billion in just the first half of 2026.

Investors are paying up for it

At the $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion valuation reportedly under discussion for its IPO, Anthropic would be worth $283 million to $377 million per employee. That's two to three times Nvidia's $121 million, a figure that has drawn attention of its own . Palantir ( PLTR ) is at $107 million and SpaceX ( SPCX ) at $95 million.

The price range in an updated filing will set the real number. Near $2 trillion, investors would be paying close to three times Nvidia's rate per worker. Even at the low end, Anthropic would top every company on the chart.

news.Title: Advanced Energy vs. KLA: Which Semiconductor Stock Is a Better Buy?
news.Content:
Advanced Energy Industries AEIS and KLA KLAC both serve the semiconductor manufacturing equipment market. AEIS specializes in precision power solutions for semiconductor equipment, while KLA provides advanced process control and inspection solutions that help manufacturers produce increasingly complex semiconductors for AI data centers and applications. Both companies benefit from growing demand for increasingly complex semiconductors used in AI data centers and other advanced computing applications.

So, AEIS or KLAC — Which of these semiconductor stocks has the greater upside potential? Let's find out.

The Case For AEIS Stock

Advanced Energy is benefiting from robust demand for semiconductor equipment, driven by increasing investments in leading-edge memory and logic technologies. Rising etch and deposition intensity, coupled with growing complexity in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, is boosting demand for the company's precision power solutions. In the second quarter of 2026, semiconductor revenues jumped 33% year over year to a record $278 million.

The company's next-generation eVerest and eVoS plasma power platforms are gaining traction, delivering improved yield and throughput for advanced manufacturing processes. Design wins in semiconductor testing, atomic layer deposition, and thermal sensing further strengthen its competitive position. The company expects semiconductor revenues to grow nearly 50% year over year in the second half of 2026, and believes new product adoption can support market share gains into 2027 and beyond.

AEIS's strong semiconductor revenue growth, expanding product portfolio, and improving manufacturing capabilities are expected to boost top-line growth. For the third quarter of 2026, Advanced Energy expects revenues of $640 million, plus or minus $20 million.

The Case for KLAC Stock

KLA is benefiting from strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory, and advanced packaging. In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, revenues reached a record $3.66 billion, increasing 15% year over year and 7% sequentially. Management attributed the performance to rising AI infrastructure investments and greater process-control intensity across memory and advanced packaging.

Advanced packaging provides another significant growth opportunity. KLA now expects advanced packaging process-control systems revenues to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year and exceeding its previous expectation of high-50% growth. Meanwhile, Specialty Process, PCB and Component Inspection businesses are expected to grow more than 25% in calendar year 2026, supported by high-performance computing and greater package complexity.

The broader semiconductor equipment environment also remains favorable. KLA raised its calendar year 2026 wafer fabrication equipment market estimate, including advanced packaging, to the low-$150-billion range from its previous expectation of more than $140 billion. Broad-based investment across leading-edge logic, foundry, DRAM, HBM, NAND and advanced packaging is expected to sustain capacity expansion. KLA expects second-half 2026 revenues to increase roughly 20% from the first half.

Story Continues

Price Performance and Valuation of AEIS and KLAC

In the year-to-date period, shares of AEIS and KLAC have rallied 3.5% and 19.8%, respectively. The outperformance in KLAC can be attributed to strong semiconductor demand, driven by accelerating investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, leading-edge foundry/logic, memory, and advanced packaging.

Despite AEIS expanding its portfolio, the company faces customer concentration, inventory and capex execution risks, tariffs, currency swings and convertible debt complexity.

Conclusion

While both AEIS and KLAC are well-positioned to benefit from rising semiconductor and AI infrastructure investments, KLAC appears better positioned for long-term growth, supported by its leadership in process control, expanding advanced packaging opportunities, and stronger stock performance.

However, AEIS faces headwinds from customer concentration, tariff uncertainty, currency fluctuations, and execution risks tied to manufacturing expansion, which could weigh on its growth prospects.
