FormFactor, Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

FormFactor, Inc. price-eps-surprise | FormFactor, Inc. Quote

Let's see how things have shaped up for the upcoming announcement.

Factors to Drive FORM's Q3 Results

FormFactor's third-quarter 2026 top-line growth is expected to have benefited from strong foundry and logic demand, sustained DRAM activity and growing co-packaged optics (CPO) adoption. Accelerating demand for advanced probe cards used in data center CPUs, networking processors and custom AI accelerators is expected to have driven top-line growth. Increasing compute intensity associated with agentic AI workloads has been driving demand for high-performance CPUs and sophisticated semiconductor testing solutions.

FormFactor's third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from sustained DRAM probe card demand, particularly for DDR5 applications. Strong memory pricing and constrained supply have encouraged DRAM manufacturers to shift wafer production toward DDR products to capitalize on higher profitability. Although FORM anticipated a product-mix shift away from high-bandwidth memory (HBM), overall DRAM probe card revenues were expected to remain near the record second-quarter level of $85 million.

FORM's expanding relationships with leading compute providers, combined with multiple design wins at a major fabless XPU customer, are likely to have supported top-line growth in the to-be-reported quarter. Growing testing complexity for DRAM and the company's established relationships with major memory manufacturers are likely to have supported revenues in the third quarter of 2026. Increasing semiconductor manufacturing activity in Taiwan, particularly in advanced logic, GPU and custom ASIC applications, is also expected to have benefited FORM's top-line growth.

Moreover, strong demand for CPO testing solutions is expected to have driven FormFactor's third-quarter Systems segment revenues. Increasing deployment of optical interconnect technologies in AI data centers is driving demand for advanced silicon photonics testing equipment. FormFactor's leadership in early-stage photonic integrated circuit wafer testing and increasing adoption of its Triton high-volume manufacturing platform have been significant growth drivers. The company previously expected CPO revenues of $10 million to $20 million in 2026 but subsequently projected that revenues would exceed $20 million by the end of the third quarter.

FormFactor's third-quarter profitability is expected to have benefited from improved manufacturing yields, shorter production cycle times and disciplined operating spending. The company has strengthened its cost structure while increasing output from existing facilities. FORM also anticipated approximately $7-$9 million of tariff refunds during the third quarter, providing a temporary benefit of roughly 300 basis points to gross margin. However, unfavorable DRAM product mix could have partially offset these gains in the to-be-reported quarter. FormFactor continues to face manufacturing capacity constraints as demand accelerates across advanced semiconductor testing applications.

Story Continues

FORM Shares Beat Sector, Valuation Stretched

FormFactor shares have appreciated 76.6% year to date (YTD), outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 14%.

FORM has underperformed Cohu COHU but outperformed Teradyne TER and KLA KLAC, YTD. While Cohu shares have jumped 106.1%, Teradyne and KLA shares have appreciated 59.5% and 19.8%, respectively, over the same time frame.

FORM Stock's Price Performance

FORM stock is overvalued, as suggested by the Value Score of F. In terms of the forward 12-month price-to-sales (P/S), the company is trading at 6.54X compared with the broader sector's 5.47X. Shares of Cohu, Teradyne and KLA trade at 3.84X, 10.86X and 15.71X, respectively.

FORM Stock's Valuation

AI Infrastructure & Advanced Packaging Aids FORM's Prospects

FormFactor is benefiting from increasing investments in AI infrastructure, high-performance computing and advanced semiconductor packaging. The adoption of chiplet architectures in GPUs, CPUs and custom accelerators is significantly increasing semiconductor testing requirements. Each chiplet must undergo extensive testing before integration into advanced packages, creating additional demand for high-performance probe cards. The company's differentiated microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) technology enables testing at higher speeds, currents and temperatures.

Growing adoption of HBM4 and future HBM generations in AI accelerators is a tailwind. FORM's SmartMatrix full-wafer contactor technology enables simultaneous high-speed testing of hundreds of HBM stacks, improving throughput and manufacturing efficiency. The company is well-positioned to capitalize on increasing adoption of custom AI accelerators and next-generation GPUs. Rising power consumption, operating temperatures and testing complexity are encouraging customers to transition from conventional wire-based probe cards to advanced MEMS technologies. FormFactor has indicated that custom ASIC adoption of advanced MEMS probe cards is expected to accelerate from 2027.

FormFactor's manufacturing expansion in Farmers Branch, TX, is expected to strengthen its long-term growth prospects by increasing production capacity and improving manufacturing efficiency. The facility is scheduled to begin production late in the fourth quarter of 2026, with capacity ramping throughout 2027. The expansion will support growing demand for advanced MEMS probe cards used in GPUs, custom ASICs and next-generation memory products. The company's growing presence in strengthens its position in the global advanced semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem.

Conclusion

FormFactor's strong exposure to AI infrastructure, advanced packaging and growing demand for semiconductor testing solutions bodes well for its long-term prospects. However, manufacturing capacity constraints, unfavorable DRAM product mix and elevated operating expenses remain concerns. Moreover, FORM's stretched valuation and significant YTD share price appreciation limit near-term upside potential. Investors may consider holding the stock ahead of third-quarter earnings, awaiting greater clarity on sustainable margin expansion and capacity improvements.

FORM currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

news.Title: Lam Research (LRCX) vs. AMAT and KLAC: Can Strong Cash Flow and AI Demand Support Further Upside?
news.Content:
Is LRCX a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Lam Research Corporation on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on LRCX. Lam Research Corporation's share was trading at $230.10 as of October 23rd 2026. LRCX's trailing and forward P/E were 34.29 and 24.88 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

LRCX shares gained 46.65% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Applied Materials and Onto Innovation gained 63.07% and 47.94%, respectively, during the same period. Why are semiconductor equipment stocks rising so much, and is it really a good time to buy them?

Portogas D Ace/Shutterstock.com

In April, we published an article about the 10 Best AI Chip Stocks to Buy According to Hedge Funds and LRCX ranked #4 in that article. LRCX has gained modestly since then. Btw, the #1 stock in that list returned 132.30% over the same period. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick, while LRCX has yet to deliver comparable returns. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on LRCX. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX) designs and makes the equipment used to build computer chips, mainly for depositing thin layers on wafers, etching patterns into them, and cleaning them. These steps matter more as AI, high-bandwidth memory, and advanced chips require more complex manufacturing. The central investment debate around Lam Research Corporation is whether its exposure to AI-driven semiconductor spending can continue to justify a premium valuation despite cyclical risks and U.S.-China export restrictions.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

Fiscal 2026 was a strong year, with revenue up 26.0% to $23.2 billion, net income up 35.6% to $7.3 billion, and gross margin improving to 50.5%. Even so, the stock trades at about 51.8 times trailing earnings and 31.5 times forward earnings, which means investors are already paying a high price for that growth.

The bullish view is that AI is making chip manufacturing harder, and harder chips need more advanced equipment. AI chips require more sophisticated deposition and etch steps, which helps Lam Research Corporation as chipmakers expand capacity for AI, high-performance computing, and high-bandwidth memory. The results so far support this view, as revenue has grown steadily from $14.9 billion in fiscal 2024 to $18.4 billion in fiscal 2025, before rising again in fiscal 2026. The company also generated $4.9 billion in free cash flow, the cash left over after running and investing in the business.

Story Continues

Profitability adds to the case. The company keeps a 35.3% operating margin, meaning a healthy share of every sales dollar turns into profit, and it holds about $1.9 billion more in cash than debt. If chipmakers keep investing in advanced manufacturing capacity, bulls expect several more years of earnings growth, which is why investors are willing to pay a premium price for the stock.

Analysts are also positive. Shares of Lam Research Corporation trade at about $298.22, while the average analyst price target is $373.13, which suggests roughly 25% upside. Targets range widely from $290 to $500, reflecting different views on AI growth, the chip recovery, and geopolitical uncertainty. Analysts also expect earnings per share to rise from $5.76 over the past year to $9.47 over the next, a sign they see growth continuing as chip spending improves.

The main risk is a slowdown in chip capital spending. If AI demand stays strong, investors would expect higher profits, but the stock already trades at a demanding price, slightly above the peer median of 50.7 times trailing earnings, so there is little room for disappointment. Tighter U.S.-China export rules could also limit equipment sales to China, while Chinese equipment makers keep trying to replace foreign suppliers.

Another risk for the stock is that supply constraints could prevent Lam from meeting strong demand. Its equipment relies on specialized components, some sourced from a single supplier or a limited group of suppliers. Lam warns that disruptions could delay deliveries, raise costs, and hurt financial results. Finding and approving replacement suppliers can take time because components must meet demanding technical standards. Holding extra inventory offers protection but also ties up cash and creates potential losses if customer requirements change. This means rising AI orders do not automatically translate into timely revenue and cash flow. In our opinion, delivery bottlenecks could pressure Lam's margins and valuation even if chipmakers continue investing heavily.

Hedge fund positioning shows a strong signal for Lam Research Corporation. (see why Barometer Capital Management is bullish on LRCX ) As per our database, 139 hedge fund portfolios held the stock at the end of the second quarter, up from 123 in the previous quarter. That is a sizeable jump, showing institutional investors are adding to their positions at a steady pace. Among peers, Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) was held by 137 hedge funds, down from 138, while KLA Corporation (NASDAQ:KLAC) was held by 81 hedge funds, up from 71, and Onto Innovation (NYSE:ONTO) was held by 75 hedge funds, up from 67. The divergence suggests institutional investors showed the strongest increase in conviction toward Lam Research Corporation, while Applied Materials remained relatively stable with only a marginal dip in ownership, and KLA Corporation and Onto Innovation gained investor attention as funds adjusted semiconductor equipment exposure based on growth expectations, restructuring opportunities, and valuation differences.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture across the semiconductor equipment space. Short interest in Lam Research Corporation stands at 2.07% of float, compared with 1.71% for Applied Materials, Inc., 1.86% for KLA Corporation, and 7.68% for Onto Innovation Inc. The low readings for Lam Research Corporation, Applied Materials, Inc., and KLA Corporation suggest few investors are betting against them, while the higher figure for Onto Innovation Inc. points to more caution around its valuation or near-term outlook.

Valuation Analysis

LRCX's forward P/E is 24.88x. KLA Corporation, Onto Innovation Inc., and Applied Materials, Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 26.95x, 16.84x, and 21.14x, respectively. LRCX's own forward P/E was 34.97x on December 31, 2025, meaning its current valuation is approximately 29% lower. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about memory spending cycles, U.S.-China export restrictions, and whether AI-driven demand can sustain strong equipment sales. However, the historical discount appears encouraging given Lam's continued profitability and growth, although its premiums to Applied Materials and Onto Innovation mean the shares are not uniformly cheap against peers. Lam Research's fiscal 2026 revenue increased 26% to $23.2 billion, while net income rose approximately 36% to $7.3 billion and free cash flow reached roughly $4.9 billion. We believe the current valuation can be justified if earnings continue expanding at a healthy pace, without requiring the latest growth rate to persist, but a slowdown accompanied by a lower multiple would weaken returns. If Lam can maintain its technology leadership and convert high-bandwidth memory investment and increasing chip complexity into sustained earnings growth, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite its exposure to cyclical customer spending.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Lam Research Corporation (LRCX) by The Antifragile Investor in May 2025, which highlighted its semiconductor equipment moat, recurring services revenue, switching costs, and long-term positioning across advanced chip manufacturing. LRCX's stock price has appreciated by approximately 177.93% since our coverage. We believe LRCX could be a good long-term investment, as its current valuation offers an attractive entry point if AI and memory investment support sustained earnings growth through the semiconductor cycle.

Lam Research Corporation is on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds . While LRCX could offer long-term upside if AI and advanced memory demand drive sustained earnings growth, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. Factors Shaping Upcoming Results

During the quarter, Silicon Motion unveiled its MonTitan SSD Reference Design Kit, targeting AI infrastructure with high-performance, scalable storage solutions. The kit helps accelerate SSD development, enabling faster data processing, improved efficiency and optimized storage performance for demanding AI workloads, data centers and next-generation computing systems.

The company is expected to benefit from growing demand for enterprise storage solutions, AI infrastructure and automotive applications in the third quarter of 2026. Management expects revenues to increase 15-20% sequentially, supported primarily by its Ferri automotive storage products, enterprise boot drive solutions and MonTitan enterprise SSD controllers. The ongoing commercial ramp of MonTitan, coupled with healthy customer order patterns across storage solutions, is expected to support the company's near-term performance.

SIMO's embedded storage business is another potential growth driver. The company continues to gain market share in eMMC and UFS controllers as NAND suppliers focus more resources on higher-priority memory products. However, rising NAND and DRAM prices remain a potential headwind. Higher component costs are making smartphones and PCs less affordable, particularly in lower-priced segments

Story Continues

Price Performance

Key Valuation Metric

From a valuation standpoint, Silicon Motion appears to be trading at a premium relative to the industry and above its mean. Going by the price/earnings ratio, the company's shares currently trade at 12.17 forward earnings, higher than 9.6 for the industry but lower than the stock's mean of 22.81.

Investment Considerations

SIMO's expanding exposure to enterprise storage, automotive applications and AI infrastructure strengthens its long-term growth opportunity. The company's controller technology, established relationships with NAND manufacturers, and growing presence in higher-value storage solutions could help it capture demand as computing workloads become more storage-intensive. The increasing contribution of MonTitan and enterprise boot drive products also offers an opportunity to reduce dependence on consumer-oriented markets over time.

Profitability is another factor worth monitoring. Management expects the third quarter to benefit from a more favorable product mix, particularly the rising contribution of MonTitan and PCIe Gen5 controllers.

However, SIMO is exposed to volatility in the consumer market. Weak smartphone and PC demand, elevated memory prices, intense competition and uncertainty surrounding component availability could limit growth in established product categories.

End Note

Expanding enterprise storage operations, market-share gains in embedded controllers and increasing demand for automotive and AI-related storage solutions are major tailwinds as SIMO is set to release third-quarter results. Nevertheless, higher memory costs, weakness in consumer markets and the pace of enterprise product adoption remain key variables. SIMO's diversification strategy boosts prospects for the long run, but in the near term, the company demonstrates a balanced outlook. Long-term investors should hold on to the stock, but new investors should wait for a better entry point.

news.Title: Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC) Earnings Expected to Grow: What to Know Ahead of Next Week's Release
news.Content:
Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC) is expected to deliver a year-over-year increase in earnings on higher revenues when it reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. This widely-known consensus outlook gives a good sense of the company's earnings picture, but how the actual results compare to these estimates is a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price.

The stock might move higher if these key numbers top expectations in the upcoming earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 2. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $0.55 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +96.4%.

Revenues are expected to be $255.13 million, up 91.3% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 4.35% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Lattice?

For Lattice, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.60%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #3.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Lattice will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Lattice would post earnings of $0.44 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.53, delivering a surprise of +20.45%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates two times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Lattice doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

An Industry Player's Expected Results

Among the stocks in the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, Entegris (ENTG), is soon expected to post earnings of $1.04 per share for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +44.4%. This quarter's revenue is expected to be $924.45 million, up 14.5% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for Entegris has been revised 0.1% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. However, a lower Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -2.06%.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), this Earnings ESP makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Entegris will beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates three times.

news.Title: Down 22.5% in 4 Weeks, Here's Why You Should You Buy the Dip in KLA (KLAC)
news.Content:
KLA (KLAC) has been on a downward spiral lately with significant selling pressure. After declining 22.5% over the past four weeks, the stock looks well positioned for a trend reversal as it is now in oversold territory and there is strong agreement among Wall Street analysts that the company will report better earnings than they predicted earlier.

We use Relative Strength Index (RSI), one of the most commonly used technical indicators, for spotting whether a stock is oversold. This is a momentum oscillator that measures the speed and change of price movements.

RSI oscillates between zero and 100. Usually, a stock is considered oversold when its RSI reading falls below 30.

Technically, every stock oscillates between being overbought and oversold irrespective of the quality of their fundamentals. And the beauty of RSI is that it helps you quickly and easily check if a stock's price is reaching a point of reversal.

So, by this measure, if a stock has gotten too far below its fair value just because of unwarranted selling pressure, investors may start looking for entry opportunities in the stock for benefiting from the inevitable rebound.

However, like every investing tool, RSI has its limitations, and should not be used alone for making an investment decision.

Why a Trend Reversal is Due for KLAC

The RSI reading of 23.08 for KLAC is an indication that the heavy selling could be in the process of exhausting itself, so the stock could bounce back in a quest for reaching the old equilibrium of supply and demand.

The RSI value is not the only factor that indicates a potential turnaround for the stock in the near term. On the fundamental side, there has been strong agreement among the sell-side analysts covering the stock in raising earnings estimates for the current year. Over the last 30 days, the consensus EPS estimate for KLAC has increased 0.4%. And an upward trend in earnings estimate revisions usually translates into price appreciation in the near term.

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Bloom Energy, SanDisk, AMD, CoreWeave, Nebius, NVIDIA and SpaceX's
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – October 26, 2026– Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Bloom Energy BE, SanDisk SNDK, Advanced Micro Devices AMD, CoreWeave CRWV, Nebius Group NBIS, NVIDIA NVDA and SpaceX's SPCX.

The AI Rout: Sorting CapEx Fact from Fiction

Funding Fears Threaten AI Bull Market

Early in the year, investors rushed into tech stocks as AI innovations, investment, and rapid growth expectations drew attention away from the rest of the market. AI-related leaders like Bloom Energy , SanDisk and Advanced Micro Devices each soared more than 100%. However, over the past few months, Wall Street's price action has completely flipped. Although major market indices are within a hair of all-time highs, leading AI-stocks have been lackluster, with many down 50% or more off their 2026 highs.

What Caused the Destruction in AI Stocks?

Gravity & Profit Taking

First, while the correction in AI-related names is undoubtedly painful for bulls (especially those who bought near the highs), corrections of this magnitude are normal in bull markets. For example, SanDisk exploded by ~2,800% from August 2025 to June 2026. In other words, after such a massive move, profit taking is to be expected. Currently, SanDisk is testing its rising 200-day moving average, the best gauge of the long-term trend, for the first time in its history. Again, even the strongest stocks occasionally succumb to the laws of gravity.

The AI Debt Fear Narrative

More recently, selling in AI stocks has intensified amid a sharp shift in Wall Street sentiment regarding AI spending and the sustainability of debt loads. The tipping point came when neocloud leader CoreWeave saw its unsecured bonds dumped, pushing yields to a distressed 15%. In other words, the move in CoreWeave's bonds suggests fixed-income investors have far less confidence in the company's ability to meet its ballooning debt. So far in October, CoreWeave shares have plunged nearly 40%, dragging other neocloud and AI -related stocks like Nebius Group along with it.

CoreWeave, which started as a Bitcoin Mining company, pivoted to AI data centers during the 2022 crypto bear market. Today, it is a specialized AI cloud provider that rents out massive clusters of graphics processing units (GPUs) and infrastructure to companies training and running AI models. Building massive AI data centers requires heavy upfront expenses for CoreWeave because its business model demands immediate, large-scale capital spending on infrastructure and hardware before it collects cash from customer contracts.

Story Continues

The Betting Markets Tell a Different Story

I've found that betting markets are far more reliable than traditional surveys or opinions because participants have real money at risk. While many headlines suggest a CoreWeave bankruptcy is imminent, the betting markets suggest otherwise. Polymarket bettors assign only an 11% chance of a CoreWeave bankruptcy filing by the end of next year.

Jensen Huang Weighs in on Neocloud Financing Concerns

Jensen Huang is the iconic CEO of the world's largest company and the most important AI company, NVIDIA . With that in mind, investors can safely assume Huang has the best sense of what's going on in the AI industry. At the GTC conference in Berlin, Huang weighed in on the neocloud financing concerns, saying:

"Everything else will get solved when demand is high. You can't solve the absence of demand. But when demand is high, everything else will get taken care of. I am quite confident that they will find solutions. Their solution starts with the fact that they have excellent customers. Demand is really high and they just need working capital, and working capital will come."

NVIDIA is a CoreWeave partner and stakeholder.

Will AI CAPEX Continue to Grow?

The current AI buildout already the largest industrial buildout in history. Because of massive amount of capital already invested, bears are betting that AI CAPEX spending is near a peak. However, the most recent data shows that Ai spending isn't slowing; it's actually increasing at a faster rate. SpaceX's earnings call provided valuable clues. 52% of SpaceX's revenue are derived from AI.

Meanwhile, during SpaceX's Q3 2026 earnings call, CEO Elon Musk projected that annual recurring revenue (ARR) could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027. Meanwhile, Wells Fargo expects Meta's CAPEX to soar to $249 billion in 2027, up from ~$145 billion in 2026. Goldman Sachs Research now projects that hyperscaler CAPEX will soar from $768 billion in 2026 to $1.182 trillion in 2027.

Bottom Line

Despite the brutal pullbacks in AI-related stocks, debt fears are far overblown and the bullish fundamental case remains rock-solid for the foreseeable future.

news.Title: Here's What $1,000 Spread Across These 4 Memory and Storage Stocks Could Be Worth by 2030
news.Content:
In July, SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY) listed on the Nasdaq as the largest American depositary receipts (ADRs) offering in Wall Street history, raising roughly $26.5 billion. For the first time, all the companies that provide the memory for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers traded on one U.S. exchange.

That matters because AI has changed the demand equation for memory. Here is what $250 apiece in Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU), Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK), SK Hynix, and Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC) might look like by 2030.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Micron, the one with every layer covered

The reason Micron belongs in an AI portfolio is high-bandwidth memory (HMB), the stacked chips packaged right next to the graphics processing unit (GPU) inside data centers so data does not have to travel far. Micron has had its HBM4 in high-volume production since March, built specifically for Nvidia's (NASDAQ: NVDA) Vera Rubin platform, and it used a technology webinar on Oct. 21 to walk investors through what it calls a multigenerational roadmap meant to keep that lead for the next decade. What I like is that Micron also sells the slower, cheaper memory, so it gets paid at every layer of the stack. The risk with this company is one that every memory investor already knows in their gut. This industry is cyclical, and Micron's shares lost roughly half their value in the 2022 downturn. It can happen again.

Sandisk, trying to make flash less cyclical

Sandisk makes NAND flash and the solid state drives (SSD) that AI servers use to hold what engineers call the KV cache, which is essentially the model's short-term memory of a long conversation so it does not have to recompute everything. The interesting thing Sandisk is doing has less to do with chips and more to do with contracts. At its August investor day, the company said eight customers have signed multiyear agreements with committed volumes and minimum financial guarantees. That is an attempt to take the boom-and-bust out of a business that has always been boom-and-bust.

SK Hynix, the HBM leader you can finally buy

SK Hynix is the South Korean company Nvidia has leaned on longest for high-bandwidth memory. It signed a multi-year technology partnership with the chipmaker in June and shipped samples of its 12-layer HBM4E, the next generation, that same month. And here is the part that surprised me. It trades at a single-digit multiple of trailing earnings, which makes it the cheapest of the four by a wide margin. The risks are specific here too. This is a new ADR with very little trading history; there are Korean governance and tax wrinkles for U.S. holders to think about; and the company runs an NAND plant in Dalian, China, that is subject to export rules.

Story Continues

Western Digital, because the hard drive refuses to die

Western Digital builds the hard drives that hold the cold data AI keeps generating, the stuff that needs to be reachable in seconds but does not need to be fast. Chief Executive Officer Irving Tan told investors in January that the company is "pretty much sold out" for calendar 2026, with firm purchase orders from its top seven customers and long-term agreements already signed with two of them for 2027 and one for 2028. On the technology side, Western Digital's roadmap targets 100 terabytes for hard drives by 2029.

The $1,000 math

This is my own scenario, and I kept it modest, because the one thing memory investors probably should never do is extrapolate an up cycle four years out. I gave SK Hynix 20% per year for being the HBM leader with the group's cheapest valuation. Micron gets 18% for having the most complete AI memory lineup. Sandisk and Western Digital get 15% each, since both have signed multiyear supply deals that should smooth the ride without necessarily speeding it up.

Run those numbers for four years, and the $250 in SK Hynix grows to about $518, the Micron slice to roughly $485, and the Sandisk and Western Digital pieces to about $437 apiece. Put it all together, and you are looking at close to $1,880 from the original $1,000. If all four just match the market's long-run 10% average return instead, you end up at roughly $1,460.

news.Title: Chip Stocks to Buy After Their Worst Day Since June
news.Content:
Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX), which sells chipmaking equipment, reported record revenue on Oct. 21. It also said limited clean-room space and shortages of some parts would stop chipmakers and equipment companies from fully meeting demand into 2027.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped 6.7% on Oct. 22, its worst day since June 23. Lam lost 12%, Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) 6%, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) 8%, and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) 9%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But Lam was describing more demand than the industry can meet, not less. And all three chipmakers' own outlooks still point up. I think the sell-off makes all three worth buying.

Image source: Getty Images.

Lam's issue is supply, not demand

Lam's revenue rose 22% from the June quarter to $8.22 billion, up 54% year over year. And management still forecast around $8.6 billion in the December quarter.

"[T]his revenue guide would have been a bit higher if not for some near-term supply chain constraints," CFO Doug Bettinger said on the earnings call.

Lam also expects industry spending on chipmaking equipment to pass $200 billion in 2027, up from the mid-$150 billion range this year. Asked what that number would be without the constraints, Bettinger said it "would be higher."

Micron: short on clean rooms, not customers

On Sept. 30, memory maker Micron said industry supply of DRAM and NAND (the two main kinds of memory chips) should stay constrained in 2027 and 2028.

"We expect memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026," CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said in prepared remarks for that day's call.

Showing what tight supply has done for Micron, its revenue rose 31% sequentially to $54.2 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 (which ended Sept. 3), as DRAM prices climbed by a high-teens percentage and NAND prices by about 30%. Management expects another record in the fiscal first quarter of 2027, at roughly $61.5 billion, and to grow in every quarter of fiscal 2027. But the stock is off 29% from its June 25 record close, at about $856 as I write, or about 5 times earnings for fiscal 2027 on analysts' consensus. That price suggests investors expect memory profits to fall soon. Micron is predicting the opposite.

Story Continues

AMD: the upside hinges on supply

AMD is supply-limited, too. In Taipei on Oct. 6, CEO Lisa Su said it plans to substantially increase supply in 2027 and needs more advanced wafer capacity.

On AMD's August earnings call, Su said she saw nothing that gave her pause about meeting its targets. That suggests the limits Lam flagged could matter more for how far AMD beats its plan than for the plan itself. Management guided for around $13 billion in third-quarter revenue, up about 41% year over year, and expects data center sales, led by its artificial intelligence (AI) chips, to more than double next year.

AMD stock, at about $508, is 22% under its Oct. 6 record close. Shares cost around 32 times earnings, based on analysts' consensus for 2027, so the price already counts on that data center doubling.

Marvell: a higher profit target

At its Oct. 6 investor day, Marvell targeted $70 billion to $90 billion of revenue for fiscal 2031 (ending early 2031) and a non-GAAP (adjusted) operating margin of 44% to 46%. Management said the midpoint of those targets implies adjusted earnings of more than $30 a share. Marvell brought in $8.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

Its revenue growth is already picking up, from 28% year over year in the fiscal first quarter of 2027 to 37% in the fiscal second quarter (which ended Aug. 1), and management expects about $3.15 billion in fiscal third-quarter revenue, roughly 52% above the year-ago quarter.

But at about $223, shares are 22% under their Oct. 6 close. They cost about 31 times earnings, based on analysts' consensus for fiscal 2028, but only about 7 times the earnings Marvell is targeting for fiscal 2031. Of course, that target's over four years off, and Marvell depends on outside manufacturers for its chips -- the sort of chipmakers Lam says can't fully meet demand.

Is the sell-off a buying opportunity?

None of these companies has cut its outlook, and all three stocks just got cheaper.

Micron's the one I'd buy first. Tight supply is already boosting its prices, and the stock's arguably priced for a downturn its own outlook doesn't show.

AMD and Marvell are pricier growth stocks that need their plans to hold up to justify over 30 times expected earnings. I think both are worth considering here, ideally a bit at a time. After all, a slowdown in AI spending might still hit all three stocks hard.

news.Title: 韓股便宜到破紀錄 預估本益比僅4.2倍、兆美元市場首見
news.Content:
隨著人工智慧（AI）熱潮降溫、資金撤離科技股，南韓綜合指數( KOSPI ) 未來12個月預估本益比降至4.2倍。根據彭博可追溯至2006年的數據，在今年初市值超過1兆美元的18個市場中，韓國成為首個基準指數預估本益比跌破5倍的市場。

這項紀錄凸顯韓股折價程度之深。KOSPI先前曾是今年科技股漲勢的代表性指數之一，受惠於AI相關需求，半導體類股大幅走高。然而，隨著AI熱潮降溫，原本支撐行情的投資邏輯迅速逆轉，亞洲部分主要股指遭到拋售，韓股首當其衝，資金加速撤出。

在彭博涵蓋近20年的資料中，今年初市值超過1兆美元的18個市場，過去未曾有任何基準指數的預估本益比跌破5倍。如今KOSPI打破這項紀錄，顯示韓股估值已降至這批大型市場過去未曾觸及的水準。不過，這項統計範圍並不包括雅加達綜合指數。

若與印尼股市比較，韓股目前的本益比僅略高於雅加達綜合指數的一半。印尼股市正因MSCI可能將該國連降兩級而大幅下挫，韓股估值卻仍明顯低於印尼，進一步凸顯市場對韓國股票給予的低評價。

與低迷估值形成對照的是，韓國今年出口額正朝1兆美元大關邁進，SK海力士與三星電子的晶片需求依然旺盛。然而，這些基本面表現尚未扭轉投資人的悲觀情緒，市場仍不願為分享科技巨頭的獲利支付更高價格。

韓股長期以來相較全球同業存在估值折價，並非新現象。這次值得關注之處，在於韓國經濟強勁成長期間，折價不僅未見收斂，反而持續擴大，企業需求與股市評價之間的落差更加鮮明。

彭博時評作者Garfield Reynolds指出，這種情況意味著，一旦市場情緒轉向、局勢塵埃落定，韓股可能迎來一段持續領先其他市場的時期。極度壓縮的估值，因而也可能為後續反彈留下可觀空間。

不過，低估值同時是一把雙面刃。對投資人而言，真正的難題不只是韓股有多便宜，而是估值回升的轉捩點何時出現，以及在此之前，KOSPI是否還會進一步下跌，讓目前已創紀錄的本益比繼續下探。

這兩個問題目前都沒有明確答案。即使韓股已成為這批兆美元級市場中首個預估本益比跌破5倍的市場，極低估值仍未自動轉化為買進訊號。潛在反彈空間與進一步下跌的可能性並存，進場時機仍是投資人面臨的核心考驗。

news.Title: Stock-Split Watch: Is Sandisk Next?
news.Content:
The rise of Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) has been one of the biggest stories on the stock market over the past couple of years. The maker of NAND flash drives and solid-state storage drives for data centers and AI applications has been on a run that's rarely been matched in recent years.

Sandisk was a public company from 1995 to 2016, when Western Digital acquired it. Sandisk went public in February 2025 at $38 per share after spinning off from Western Digital.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

But when it went public, it hit right in the middle of the AI storage supercycle, with demand far outpacing supply. This created insatiable demand for Sandisk's drives and allowed it to have a huge amount of pricing power. The combination produced an earnings powerhouse.

Investors started piling into Sandisk stock, and over the course of its roughly a year and a half as a public company, the stock price soared 3,136% to the current price of $1,246 per share. On an annualized basis, this comes to an average return of 718% over the past 18 months since the IPO.

And as wild as that is, Sandisk stock had peaked at $2,335 per share on June 25, which, at the time, was some 6,500% above the price it debuted at.

Stock-split time

The meteoric rise of Sandisk makes it a candidate for a stock split. When stock prices reach four-digit territory, companies often decide to split their stock.

With a stock split , a single share is split into multiple shares -- how many depends on the company.

This year, we saw a massive 25-for-1 stock split by Booking Holdings on April 2. That meant that every one share of Booking stock, which traded at a whopping $4,250 per share at the time of the split, was split into 25 shares. That brought the price down to around $170 per share.

CrowdStrike also conducted a 4-for-1 stock split on July 2. That brought the CrowdStrike share price from $774 per share before the split to around $193 per share.

Companies typically conduct stock splits to attract new investors by lowering the share price. They may also do it to provide employees with stock-based compensation or to lower their share price for stock repurchases. Sometimes it does help boost the share price, like with Booking, which surged about 10% in the two weeks after the split to $191 per share. But that's not always the case.

Story Continues

Sandisk management has made no mention of splitting its stock price, so it's pure speculation at this point. But based on its huge revenue projections amid the ongoing storage supercycle, analysts expect Sandisk stock to soar another 77% over the next 12 months to $2,225 per share. If that's the case, Sandisk should be a strong candidate for a stock split sometime within the next year.

news.Title: 聯發科TPU進度遭質疑！ 花旗法說前送暖：目標上看6800元
news.Content:
面對市場對聯發科TPU發展的疑慮，花旗證券於法說前夕出面力挺，看好受惠於AI ASIC貢獻與消費性產品漲價，第四季營收將迎來約30%的強勁季增，重申買進評等並維持目標價6,800元。

法說前夕送暖力挺

IC設計龍頭廠聯發科（2454）預計於10月30日召開線上法人說明會，公佈第三季財務報告與第四季業績展望。儘管近期市場對於聯發科的張量處理器（TPU）開發與新專案進展存有疑慮，但花旗證券在最新研究報告中發布正面看法，認為營運長線成長趨勢依舊明確，並給予正面評價。

AI ASIC與消費產品雙引擎

花旗分析指出，聯發科的v8專案正按計畫順利推進，今年超過20億美元的營收貢獻，將成為帶動第四季營收季增長的核心催化劑。結合消費性產品的價格調漲與產品組合改善，預期第四季營收可獲得約30%的季增表現，且在營運槓桿效益帶動下，營業利益率亦具備上行空間。

先進封裝與技術佈局延伸

針對市場對EMIB-T技術面臨良率挑戰與週期較長所引發的v9生產風險疑慮，花旗表示此狀況已在預料之中。然而，受惠於v8專案的長期成長動能，加上SerDes升級與N2製程開發帶動平均售價提升，花旗維持2028年AI ASIC營收貢獻達400億美元的預測。技術進展方面，聯發科除已量產的224G SerDes外，336G與448G SerDes也在積極開發中。此外，針對瞄準2029年量產的TPU v10，聯發科有很大機會採用CoWOS或CoPoS封裝技術，相關訂單能見度已延伸至2029年之後。

生態系合作與財務預估上調

花旗強調，聯發科憑藉先進製程設計能力、SerDes開發技術、供應鏈管理能力及靈活的商業模式，有極大機會進一步滲透至新的雲端服務供應商專案中。同時，聯發科亦為NVLink Fusion生態系中，少數具備前端設計與全流程AI ASIC服務能力的重要玩家，將為2028年之後帶來長遠發展契機。基於營運槓桿與AI ASIC的爆發性成長，花旗將聯發科2026年、2027年及2028年的獲利預估分別調升9%、25%與9%，並重申「買進」評等目標價6,800元。

（封面圖／翻攝《MediaTek》粉專）

news.Title: 5 big analyst AI moves: ’Uniquely catalyst-rich’ months ahead for SpaceX
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Here are the biggest analyst moves in the area of artificial intelligence (AI) for this week.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Loop Capital downgrades Apple after supply chain checks reveal no iPhone recovery plan

Brokerage firm Loop Capital this week downgraded Apple to Hold from Buy and cut its price target to $330 from $370, after supply chain checks revealed Apple has no plans to recover the 13 million iPhone shipments cut in the second half of 2026.

Analyst Ananda Baruah said Apple previously reduced September- and December-quarter iPhone shipments by 10%, with Loop having initially believed those units could be made up through 2027 as the reductions were supply-related rather than demand-driven.

"This no longer appears to be the case," Baruah wrote.

Loop lowered its December-quarter iPhone unit forecast to 79 million from the Street's 85 million, cutting its average selling price (ASP) estimate to $1,123 from $1,239. For calendar 2027, it raised its unit forecast to 260 million but cut ASP to $1,096 from $1,235, lowering iPhone revenue to $285 billion from $315 billion and trimming EPS to $9.76 from $10.11.

The broker also flagged potential gross margin risk as memory costs keep rising, lowering its normalized EPS estimate to $11 from $12 and applying Apple's median P/E of 30 times to arrive at the new target.

"We continue to like AAPL's longer-term share gain and Services story… but believe the stock also requires a fundamental catalyst reset after its recent stock appreciation," Baruah said.

JPMorgan upgrades Intel as pullback from peak makes risk-reward more balanced

JPMorgan has upgraded Intel to Neutral from Underweight, saying the risk/reward is now much more balanced as the stock approaches the bank's $85 price target after pulling back roughly 40% from its June peak, compared with a 20-25% decline for the broader chip group.

Analyst Harlan Sur noted that since JPMorgan downgraded the stock in November 2022, Intel's server x86 CPU revenue share has fallen from 77% to 53% and its PC CPU share from 81% to 68%, with a few more quarters of share losses expected, particularly in server CPUs.

In foundry, Intel appears to be making strong inroads on yields and new customer engagements, though it generated barely $1 billion in annualized external foundry revenue in the first half of 2026, compared with $150 billion for TSMC.

Sur said that since Lip Bu Tan became CEO, execution has improved in Intel's core client and data center compute markets and in next-generation manufacturing. "Despite near-term concerns on AI infrastructure spending sustainability, we believe increasing agentic AI workloads (CPU intensive) and a very tight supply chain for leading edge silicon should drive continued positive EPS revisions in the upcoming earnings season and through CY27," he wrote.

Story Continues

JPMorgan's 2028 EPS estimates sit about 15% above consensus.

"Risk/reward is more balanced at current levels and we move to a Neutral rating," Sur said.

Citi opens positive Catalyst Watch on SpaceX, sees coming months as "uniquely catalyst-rich"

Earlier in the week, Citi opened a positive 90-day Catalyst Watch on SpaceX, arguing the coming months will be "uniquely catalyst rich," after the company reported revenue that more than doubled in the third quarter and posted net income of $4.4 billion, its first profitable quarter as a public company.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Growth was driven largely by SpaceX's AI segment, with space and connectivity businesses also expanding. CEO Elon Musk also offered some of his most detailed comments yet on a potential merger with Tesla, saying the move would be "a good idea" and confirming for the first time that special committees had been formed to discuss a potential union.

Musk said he expects annual recurring revenue (ARR) to reach between $500 billion and $1 trillion by end-2027, driven by surging demand for data-center space amid the AI boom.

Citi, which rates the stock Buy, pointed to six factors behind its positive catalyst watch: SpaceX's "track record of beats/raises" expected to continue into the fourth quarter; Flight 15 as "a monumental space-industry catalyst that sets the stage for rapid reusability on a scale never before demonstrated in launch"; dollar-per-watt economics "trending significantly above consensus expectations"; an accelerated Grok model release cadence; the possibility of more detail on SpaceX's power-generation solutions before year-end; and further clarity on its "evolving mobile strategy."

"We've described Buy-rated SPCX as being in the midst of a catalyst-rich 2-3 year arc, and we see the next 2-3 months in particular as uniquely catalyst rich even within that timeline that supports our positive investment thesis," Citi analysts said.

Buy Lam Research on pullback, Mizuho says

Mizuho has reiterated its Outperform rating on Lam Research and recommended buying the stock after a significant pullback following quarterly results, trimming its price target to $360 from $365.

Analyst Vijay Rakesh highlighted that Lam expects wafer fab equipment (WFE) spending to grow more than 29% in 2027 to over $200 billion, after rising about 42% to roughly $155 billion this year. "We are buyers on the pullback, as new greenfield fabs, NAND/HBM/Terafab position for upside," he wrote, also flagging Tesla's comments pointing to "10s of $B WFE" from Terafab in early 2028 and $100 billion long-term.

Mizuho highlighted the emergence of SLC NAND as a major tailwind, with each 1 percentage point mix shift requiring 2% more NAND wafer capacity — a market where Lam holds about 90% share. NAND revenue rose 38% in the September quarter and foundry grew 28%. The broker estimates Lam's revenue will grow 37% next year, ahead of 30% consensus, and believes Lam sees 10 new tier 1 fabs coming online in 2027.

"We see LRCX well positioned with: 1) wide competitive moats, 2) secular technology trends with HPC/AI/ML, HBM/CoWoS/TSV, GAA/BPD, and 3) rising capital intensity at the leading edge," Rakesh said.

Lam reported September-quarter revenue of $8.22 billion and EPS of $2.20, broadly in line with consensus, with gross margin rising 40 basis points sequentially to 52.4%. December-quarter guidance of $8.6 billion in revenue and EPS of $2.33 came in slightly above expectations.

AI bubble exists but will not burst yet: Yardeni

This week, Financial research firm Yardeni Research introduced an AI Bubble Meter, built using Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1, which it says confirms a bubble exists in AI-related stocks but shows it is not yet close to bursting.

The tool has two dials. The Conditions dial measures whether a bubble exists by drawing on the setups that preceded the 1999-2000 tech bust and the 2006-2007 housing bust, and currently reads 83 out of 100. The Triggers dial tracks whether the forces that ended past booms — a credit boom and a sustained rise in the cost of capital — are underway, and reads just 34.

"The meter says there's a bubble, but it's not about to burst," Yardeni wrote.

One trigger has kicked in, with the two-year Treasury yield up 115 basis points from its December low, but credit is not stretched outside AI-related areas of the economy. "The preconditions of a bubble are in place and have been for a while, but the forces that ended past booms are only partially present," the firm said.

Yardeni noted that since 1965, quarters with high Conditions and low Triggers readings were followed by an S&P 500 bear market within two years only 9% of the time, with a median inflation-adjusted gain of 18.3% over that period. When both dials read high, the odds of a bear market rose to 42% with a median loss of 12.5%.

"But the Triggers dial is the one to watch: If it starts rising toward High, so do the risks," Yardeni said, flagging the two-year yield and signs of idle capacity in hyperscalers' third-quarter results as key things to monitor.

news.Title: Sandisk's New Business Model Is Transforming the Business. Now Is the Time to Buy the Stock.
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) makes NAND memory chips, which are primarily used for long-term data storage in devices like solid-state drives. That may sound like a pretty boring business with not a lot of innovation going on in it -- and you'd be right.

That's why Sandisk and its peers are normally pretty boring stocks, but all of that changed in 2026. Demand for storage skyrocketed alongside data center build-outs, consuming all available production capacity. All of a sudden, Sandisk's products were hot commodities, and prices skyrocketed, which translated into incredible stock growth for Sandisk.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

It's up nearly 500% this year -- second-best in the S&P 500 . This also allowed Sandisk to form a new, sustainable business model. I think the transition to this model will help Sandisk tremendously over the long term and eliminate some of the cyclicality typically associated with companies in the memory chip industry.

That completely flips the narrative behind investing in Sandisk's stock, making this an ideal time to buy it.

Sandisk isn't as dependent on market conditions

In normal times with ample supply, there isn't a lot that separates Sandisk's storage devices from its competition, so only one thing matters: price. The lowest price wins here, which isn't the greatest for Sandisk as a business.

However, with sky-high demand and no supply, Sandisk is taking this opportunity to reformulate its business model. The aptly named "New Business Model (NBM)" is basically a contractual agreement with some clients that sets a floor and ceiling for memory prices but has committed volumes. This is a key development, because it makes Sandisk's future more predictable.

Consistent cash flows allow the management team to allocate capital where they see fit, rather than worrying about what the business will look like a few years down the road. That's why subscription business models are king, as they are predictable. With Sandisk moving toward contract-based work, this will help smooth out the demand curve and reduce cyclical drawdowns that have plagued investors in this industry.

However, the stock is still priced like it's due for a cyclical drawdown.

SNDK PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

Remember: 6.3 times forward earnings is a dirt cheap price tag to pay for any stock. Sandisk's business model shifting more toward consistent contract work, so this should result in an increased stock premium, as it won't be as dependent on price swings in the market.

Story Continues

I think the opportunity is compelling enough to warrant buying shares now , and investors should act before the market catches up to this transformation.

news.Title: Micron vs. Sandisk: Which Is the Better AI Memory Stock to Own for the Next 3 Years
news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) have delivered stellar returns so far this year, driven by the incredible demand for memory chips deployed in artificial intelligence (AI) data centers.

While Micron stock has jumped by more than 3x in 2026, clocking a 220% jump as of this writing, Sandisk's gains are even more impressive at 480%. Of course, both stocks have experienced volatility lately, but the strong fundamentals of the memory market suggest that they can step on the gas once again.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

We will take a closer look at the prospects of Micron and Sandisk in this article to find out which memory stock could deliver bigger gains to investors over the next three years.

Micron enjoys an edge over Sandisk

Though Sandisk stock has outperformed Micron this year, investors will do well to note that the latter is in a better position to capitalize on the memory boom. That's because Micron sells both dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash storage products. Sandisk, meanwhile, is a pure-play NAND flash manufacturer.

Micron, therefore, is benefiting from the massive surge in demand for both DRAM and NAND flash. Specifically, the DRAM business produced 73% of Micron's top line in the previous quarter, reaching almost $40 billion in revenue. Micron's exposure to the DRAM business allows the company to capitalize on the fast-growing high-bandwidth memory (HBM) space, where both volumes and shipments are rising rapidly.

Micron management noted on the latest earnings call that HBM sales are growing faster than conventional DRAM sales. That isn't surprising, as HBM plays a central role in quickly transporting huge data sets in AI chip clusters, ensuring that accelerator chips don't sit idle waiting for data. Even better, strong HBM demand is fueling Micron's bottom-line growth. The company notes that it has raised HBM pricing "significantly" for 2027, suggesting that its strong earnings growth rate is sustainable.

Additionally, semiconductor equipment giant ASML recently noted that supply shortages in the memory industry are widening in both size and time horizon. Similarly, SK Hynix estimates that DRAM undersupply will widen in 2027, and new capacity will only come online in June 2029. As such, Micron's DRAM business is poised for healthy growth over the next three years.

Story Continues

On the other hand, the NAND flash market is also expected to remain undersupplied for the next three years. This is great news for both Micron and Sandisk. Chinese NAND flash company YMTC recently noted that the NAND flash shortage is likely to persist until the end of 2029.

It is easy to see why demand for NAND flash is poised to substantially exceed supply. AI data centers require a lot of storage to store enormous data sets needed to train AI models and continuously feed data for inference and agentic AI applications. Given that traditional hard-disk drives (HDDs) are reportedly in short supply until 2028, AI data centers are turning to enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs).

However, the phenomenal demand for enterprise SSDs has led to a massive price spike. Tom's Hardware reported in August that the price of a 30TB enterprise SSD has surged by 6.5x in just a year. The strong pricing environment is likely to continue for the next three years amid the ongoing supply shortage.

Also, smartphone and personal computer (PC) shipments are declining due to high memory costs. This will create strong pent-up demand in the coming years, indicating that the improvement in Sandisk and Micron's margins will continue. Micron, however, has an additional catalyst in the form of the DRAM market, which explains why it is anticipated to deliver stronger bottom-line growth than Sandisk.

The verdict

Though Sandisk is a pure-play NAND flash company, its market share of 11% is lower than Micron's 15%, according to Counterpoint Research. Additionally, Micron's share of the NAND flash market improved by two percentage points year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while Sandisk maintained its share.

Meanwhile, Micron has 24% DRAM market share, and its share increased by two percentage points year over year in Q2. All this explains why analysts are expecting Micron's earnings per share to grow at a faster pace in the long run compared to Sandisk.

YCharts

What's more, Micron is the cheaper semiconductor stock to buy right now.

So, Micron clearly seems like a much better growth stock to buy and hold over the next three years to benefit from the memory boom. It is more attractively valued, is present in both the DRAM and NAND flash markets, and is likely to grow at a significantly faster pace than Sandisk. These factors could help Micron outperform Sandisk over the next three years.

news.Title: Micron and Sandisk Hit Record Memory Margins. There's One Clear Winner.
news.Content:
Being a memory chip stock investor during 2026 has been incredibly rewarding. Two of the best performers are Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU), and each has delivered impressive returns over the past year. The reason is simple: Memory chip demand is at an all-time high, and supply has run out. Therefore, prices on memory chips have skyrocketed. This has been massively beneficial to Sandisk's and Micron's profit pictures, and each has achieved record margins.

While both stocks are doing quite well, I think there's one clear winner here, and it has far more upside moving forward.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Micron and Sandisk are thriving in today's environment

Micron and Sandisk both make memory chips, but the areas they focus on are different. Both Sandisk and Micron make NAND memory, which is used for long-term data storage, often in devices like solid-state drives. Micron also makes DRAM memory, which is used for quick information access in computing devices. Both of these are important, but one segment of Micron's business stands out.

A subsegment of DRAM memory is HBM -- high bandwidth memory. HBM is what is used inside computing units like graphics processing units (GPUs), and Micron points out that industry HBM shipments will grow at a faster pace than conventional DRAM. For 2027 and 2028, Micron expects industry NAND and DRAM shipments to grow in the low to mid-20% range both years. So, there isn't going to be a lot of growth in these two industries, but with HBM growing faster than DRAM, it will give Micron an edge over Sandisk.

Micron also announced an industry-first partnership: a custom HBM chip for Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA). This is a big deal, as Nvidia and its peers were just using off-the-shelf memory chips. But with Micron entering into a partnership with Nvidia, this could lead to a more contractual situation, stabilizing Micron's revenue.

This is an issue for both Sandisk and Micron, as unstable revenue and cash flows are common in the industry. Memory chips are cyclical, and prices can rise and fall with demand. You can see this come to life in Micron's and Sandisk's profit margins, as they are highest when demand is great -- like it is right now.

YCharts.

Both companies are taking steps to mitigate the effects of a downturn by entering into long-term supply agreements with their clients. Basically, Micron and Sandisk are trading the upside of higher memory chip prices for guaranteed revenue. This reduces the ceiling, but also raises the floor of business performance. Since this industry has been plagued by prolonged underperformance due to low demand, this is a smart move. Micron estimates it has now secured about 35% of its revenue through 2030. Sandisk has signed about 50% of its clients to these kinds of contracts.

Story Continues

This is a major evolution for both companies, and it could lead the market to value their stocks higher.

Micron and Sandisk are both cheap

Because the market is expecting a cyclical downturn from both companies at any moment, their stocks don't trade at very high premiums.

YCharts. PE = price-to-earnings.

However, with both companies taking steps to close their cyclical potential, I think they should trade at a nearly average premium for big tech stocks. If they can rally to something like 20 times earnings by the end of their respective fiscal years, that could lead to the stocks tripling or quadrupling in value by this time next year.

That's a huge performance, but that will only occur if the market understands that these two have fundamentally shifted their business to be less exposed to cyclical downturns.

So, which is the winner? I think it's clearly Micron . Micron has exposure to HBM, which will be the highest growth area within the memory chip industry. It's also trading at a far cheaper price tag than Sandisk, giving it more upside. While Sandisk is still a solid pick, Micron offers greater return potential.

news.Title: 聯電ADR23日上漲0.36美元漲幅1.94%折台股122.82元
Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
news.Content:
By Lewis Krauskopf

NEW YORK, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US stock investors face a pivotal week, with corporate earnings reports led by major AI players and a Federal Reserve meeting posing critical tests for a suddenly shaky market rally.

Weakness in technology shares left investors on edge about the state of the AI trade that has ‌driven the US equity bull market that just marked its fourth anniversary.

The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss on Friday, a day after the tech-heavy index suffered ‌its biggest daily drop since June. Investors were disappointed by quarterly reports from Meta and Lam Research. Meta is one of the hyperscalers spending massively to build out data centers, while Lam is a high-flying semiconductor company, one of ​a group that has been among the biggest AI stock winners.

Three other hyperscalers -- Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon -- headline a packed week of quarterly results, including about one-third of S&P 500 companies. The Fed's interest rate policy meeting on Wednesday also could rattle markets.

"There are a lot of balls in the air," said Nick Giorgi, chief equity strategist at Alpine Macro.

"Next week, you have a lot more tech earnings, and right now the market is taking a discerning eye as it relates to all the spending that goes along with artificial intelligence," Giorgi said. "The market's just not giving the benefit of ‌the doubt to companies that are spending a ton of money ⁠on building this all out, which to us is actually very healthy, but still does augur for some short-term pain."

Investors also have their focus trained on the US midterm elections on November 3, with growing bets that the Democrats will wrest control of the US Congress away from President Donald ⁠Trump's Republican party. The series of market catalysts could ratchet up volatility over the next couple of weeks and challenge optimism that has helped lift the benchmark S&P 500 index up 11% in 2026.

HYPERSCALERS ON THE HOT SEAT

Robust US profit growth has underpinned the stock market's gains this year in the face of headwinds including spiking Treasury yields and rising energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict.

With more than ​100 ​companies having posted results so far, third-quarter S&P 500 earnings are on pace to have climbed more than ​32% from a year ago, according to LSEG IBES data. Next week ‌is the busiest of the reporting season.

"I think earnings will determine whether this ... tech pullback is a buying opportunity, or is there a deeper correction ahead," said King Lip, chief strategist at BakerAvenue Wealth Management. "What we need is just another round of really strong earnings."

Story Continues

Alphabet and Microsoft report on Wednesday. Amazon's results are due Thursday. Focus will be on the guidance the companies give on capital spending plans and whether they are seeing returns on the massive outlays.

Capital spending from hyperscalers, expected to be around $800 billion this year, is boosting the bottom lines for a wide swath of companies involved in the AI buildout. But investors are wary of the sustainability of such spending amid mounting financing costs.

"Earnings are critical to the overall confidence level of the ‌AI trade and how much longer the spend will continue," said Kevin Mahn, president and chief investment officer ​at Hennion & Walsh Asset Management.

FED EXPECTED TO PAUSE ON RATES, FOR NOW

Quarterly reports next week from chip companies Intel ​and Sandisk also could influence the AI trade.

Elsewhere, other high-profile companies set to report ​next week include drugmaker Eli Lilly, oil majors Exxon and Chevron and industrial equipment giant Caterpillar.

The prospect for more interest rate hikes also comes into ‌focus with the Fed meeting. The Fed raised rates in September for ​the first time since 2023, in an effort ​to control above-target inflation, but Fed funds futures late on Friday suggested a less-than 10% chance the Fed will hike again when it gives its policy statement on Wednesday, according to LSEG data.

One factor: Investors are dubious that the Fed will want to increase rates just a week before the midterm elections.

However, markets are leaning toward a hike ​at the next meeting in December, with futures suggesting a roughly ‌80% probability of such a move then.

Walter Todd, chief investment officer at Greenwood Capital, said he will be watching for any hints about the rate path at Fed ​Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference following the decision.

"Does he say something to give an idea about December, because right now the expectation is there is going ​to be a hike," Todd said.

(Reporting by Lewis Krauskopf, editing by Colin Barr and David Gregorio)

SanDisk Corp. ( SNDK , Financials ), the flash-memory business, gained roughly 4% in premarket trade after falling 8.5% .A selloff in semiconductor and memory equities followed Tesla's decreased capital-spending estimate for 2026 and a worse forecast from Lam Research connected to supply-chain bottlenecks.SanDisk's next big catalyst will be fiscal first-quarter results on Oct. 29. news.Content:
Investing.com -- SK Hynix's decision to scrap plans for a U.S. initial public offering of its Solidigm business could benefit Micron Technology and Sandisk by reducing the risk of additional NAND flash supply entering the market, according to LYNX Equity Strategies.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The analyst team led by KC Rajkumar said in an Oct. 23 note that a U.S. IPO would have provided Solidigm with capital to finance additional NAND manufacturing capacity in the United States. That expansion could have increased global supply in three or more years, potentially putting pressure on prices and competing suppliers.

With the IPO scrapped, that potential source of funding has disappeared, reducing the prospect of a capacity expansion that could have weighed on NAND prices. "The overhang of new capacity addition to the global supply of NAND flash has been eliminated," LYNX wrote.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The proposed U.S. facility was expected to involve a joint venture between SK Hynix and Intel, potentially at Intel's Ohio campus. LYNX said the news would ordinarily represent a material positive for Micron and Sandisk, both NAND suppliers, as a lower risk of future capacity growth could support industry pricing and valuations. However, the team cautioned that the current market environment could limit any share-price gains despite the favorable supply implications.

Intel, meanwhile, could face a minor negative from the decision, as the abandoned plan removes a potential manufacturing project for its Ohio campus.

The broader implication for memory stocks is that the cancellation reduces a potential source of future competition, rather than immediately changing existing NAND supply. Any benefit to Micron and Sandisk will depend on how the industry's capacity plans and supply-demand balance evolve.

news.Title: The AI Rout: Sorting CAPEX Fact From Fiction
news.Content:
Funding Fears Threaten AI Bull Market

Early in the year, investors rushed into tech stocks as AI innovations, investment, and rapid growth expectations drew attention away from the rest of the market. AI-related leaders like Bloom Energy ( BE ), SanDisk ( SNDK ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) each soared more than 100%. However, over the past few months, Wall Street's price action has completely flipped. Although major market indices are within a hair of all-time highs, leading AI-stocks have been lackluster, with many down 50% or more off their 2026 highs.

What Caused the Destruction in AI Stocks?

Gravity & Profit Taking

First, while the correction in AI-related names is undoubtedly painful for bulls (especially those who bought near the highs), corrections of this magnitude are normal in bull markets. For example, SanDisk exploded by ~2,800% from August 2025 to June 2026. In other words, after such a massive move, profit taking is to be expected. Currently, SanDisk is testing its rising 200-day moving average, the best gauge of the long-term trend, for the first time in its history. Again, even the strongest stocks occasionally succumb to the laws of gravity.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The AI Debt Fear Narrative

More recently, selling in AI stocks has intensified amid a sharp shift in Wall Street sentiment regarding AI spending and the sustainability of debt loads. The tipping point came when neocloud leader CoreWeave ( CRWV ) saw its unsecured bonds dumped, pushing yields to a distressed 15%. In other words, the move in CoreWeave's bonds suggests fixed-income investors have far less confidence in the company's ability to meet its ballooning debt. So far in October, CoreWeave shares have plunged nearly 40%, dragging other neocloud and AI -related stocks like Nebius Group ( NBIS ) along with it.

CoreWeave, which started as a Bitcoin Mining company, pivoted to AI data centers during the 2022 crypto bear market. Today, it is a specialized AI cloud provider that rents out massive clusters of graphics processing units (GPUs) and infrastructure to companies training and running AI models. Building massive AI data centers requires heavy upfront expenses for CoreWeave because its business model demands immediate, large-scale capital spending on infrastructure and hardware before it collects cash from customer contracts.

The Betting Markets Tell a Different Story

I've found that betting markets are far more reliable than traditional surveys or opinions because participants have real money at risk. While many headlines suggest a CoreWeave bankruptcy is imminent, the betting markets suggest otherwise. Polymarket bettors assign only an 11% chance of a CoreWeave bankruptcy filing by the end of next year.

Story Continues

Jensen Huang Weighs in on Neocloud Financing Concerns

Jensen Huang is the iconic CEO of the world's largest company and the most important AI company, NVIDIA ( NVDA ). With that in mind, investors can safely assume Huang has the best sense of what's going on in the AI industry. At the GTC conference in Berlin, Huang weighed in on the neocloud financing concerns, saying:

"Everything else will get solved when demand is high. You can't solve the absence of demand. But when demand is high, everything else will get taken care of. I am quite confident that they will find solutions. Their solution starts with the fact that they have excellent customers. Demand is really high and they just need working capital, and working capital will come."

NVIDIA is a CoreWeave partner and stakeholder.

Will AI CAPEX Continue to Grow?

The current AI buildout already the largest industrial buildout in history. Because of massive amount of capital already invested, bears are betting that AI CAPEX spending is near a peak. However, the most recent data shows that Ai spending isn't slowing; it's actually increasing at a faster rate. SpaceX's ( SPCX ) earnings call provided valuable clues. 52% of SpaceX's revenue are derived from AI.

Meanwhile, during SpaceX's Q3 2026 earnings call, CEO Elon Musk projected that annual recurring revenue (ARR) could reach $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027. Meanwhile, Wells Fargo expects Meta's CAPEX to soar to $249 billion in 2027, up from ~$145 billion in 2026. Goldman Sachs Research now projects that hyperscaler CAPEX will soar from $768 billion in 2026 to $1.182 trillion in 2027.

Image Source: Goldman Sachs Research

Bottom Line

Despite the brutal pullbacks in AI-related stocks, debt fears are far overblown and the bullish fundamental case remains rock-solid for the foreseeable future.

Increased investments in DRAM manufacturing, particularly high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI accelerators and data centers, are expected to have driven top-line growth in the fiscal first quarter. Growing HBM adoption, increasing extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography applications and rising memory-device complexity are creating additional demand for process control equipment. HBM's larger die sizes, stringent performance specifications and complex stacking architectures require more sophisticated inspection and metrology capabilities. These factors bode well for KLAC.

Moreover, fiscal first-quarter results are expected to have benefited from robust demand for advanced packaging solutions, supported by growing adoption of heterogeneous integration, chiplets and high-performance computing architectures. Increasing packaging complexity is encouraging semiconductor manufacturers to deploy more advanced inspection and metrology tools to improve yields and manufacturing efficiency.
